notes: Optionally add jalapeños too.

all_ingredients_flat: firm tofu, turmeric powder, paprika, tahini, nutritional yeast, plant-based milk, kala namak (Himalayan Black Salt), red onion, jalapeño, Ezekiel 4:9 bread
instructions:
WET MIXTURE: In a bowl, combine 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, 1/2 tsp paprika, 1 Tbsp tahini, 2 Tbsp nutritional yeast and 1/2 cup plant-based milk of our choice. Optionally add 1/4 tsp kala namak (Himalayan Black Salt) for flavor. Stir well into a creamy mixture. Set aside.
COOK: In a pan, sauté crumbled tofu with 1/2 cup red onion (finely chopped) and 1 jalapeño (minced) for a few minutes. Then add the Wet Mixture set aside to cooked tofu. Mix well and cook for a few more minutes. Scrambled tofu is ready!
serving_suggestion: On Ezekiel 4:9 bread!

creator: Dr Sirisha Potluri
all_ingredients_flat: sprouted whole wheat flour, salt, flaxseed powder, baking powder, plain unsweetened soy milk, hot water, tofu, green bell pepper, green onions, carrots, red onion, garlic, cumin powder, green chilies, coriander leaves, raisins, cashews, almonds, walnuts
instructions: DOUGH: In a large bowl, mix together dry ingredients (sprouted whole wheat flour, flaxseed powder, baking powder & salt). Add hot soy milk (or any plain unsweetened plant milk) and hot water, a little bit at a time to the dry mixture. Knead to make soft, pliable dough. Keep kneading dough for a couple of minutes until it is smooth and elastic. Use the fold, press and knead motion to make the dough smooth. Divide dough into 10-12 equal portions. Cover and let it rest. STUFFING: Dice and grate all the veggies. Crumble tofu with your hands. Heat a thick bottom pan. Sauté green chili & garlic for 30 seconds. Slowly add the rest of the veggies and cook them for 2-3 mins. Add crumbled tofu. Mix well and cook for a few more mins. Add cumin seed powder, raisins & mixed nuts powder. Mix well & switch off the stove. Let the mixture cool. POCKETS: ROLL: Dust each portion of dough in flour. Flatten it using a rolling pin into circular shapes (approximately 8 inch diameter). Dust with flour in between to prevent the dough from sticking to the surface. STUFF & SHAPE: Place 1-2 Tbsp of cooked Stuffing (tofu & veggie mix) in the middle. Then fold into pockets, as shown in the picture, applying a little bit of water to the edges. COOK: Heat stuffed pockets on a non stick pan until they are 3/4th cooked. Then bake (15-20 mins at 375 F) or air fry (5-8 mins at 350 F) these pockets and serve them warm! STORE: Leftovers refrigerate well for 3-4 days. Reheat in air fryer or oven.
serving_suggestion: serve them warm!
notes: Leftovers refrigerate well for 3-4 days. Reheat in air fryer or oven.

all_ingredients_flat: Brown rice, Grated coconut, Black eyed peas, Mustard seeds, Asafetida, Green chilli, Curry leaves, Salt, Water
instructions:
BLACK EYED PEAS: Soak in water for some time, cook & drain.

(1) Heat a dry pan, add half a teaspoon of mustard seeds and let it splutter.
(2) Add asafetida, chopped green chillies, and curry leaves.
(3) Add 1.5 cups of water and salt to taste and bring it to boil.

all_ingredients_flat: Grated pumpkin or squash, Ezekiel bread crumbs, Tiger nut flour, Date sugar, Himalayan salt, Hing (asafoetida), Green chillies, Water, Banana leaves, Fox nuts
instructions:
1) Mix all the ingredients together. Add water to bind the mixture into a soft, dough like consistency.
2) Heat a cast iron skillet at low heat. Pat a fist sized ball of the mixture and flatten it on a banana leaf in the shape of Bhakri.
3) Place the banana leaf with Bhakri on the skillet. Cover it with another banana leaf on top. Cook on low heat until the banana leaf at the bottom chars.
4) Discard the charred banana leaf. Flip the Bhakri and cook on the second banana leaf (which was on top earlier).
5) Once the second banana leaf chars, discard it. Flip the Bhakri again and cook until it is evenly cooked.
6) Enjoy Bhakri with your favorite chutneys :))
TIP: If banana leaves are not available, we may cook Bhakri with the lid on, flipping a few times to cook both sides.

creator: Ankit Dangi
all_ingredients_flat: chana dal, toor dal, yellow split masoor dal, green split moong dal, black split urad dal, white urad dal, ginger, byadagi chilli, dried prunes, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, carom seeds, fennel seeds, asafoetida (hing), kale stems, leeks, arugula, cilantro, curry leaves, green chillies, water, fenugreek seeds, red onions, baby bok choy
instructions: SOAKING: 1/4 cup each of chana dal, toor dal, yellow split masoor dal, green split moong dal, black split urad dal, and white urad dal — wash, rinse & soak in water for 2 hours. BATTER: In a blender, add 1 inch ginger, 2 byadagi chilli, 3 dried prunes, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp carom seeds, 1 tsp fennel seeds, a pinch of asafoetida (hing), 5-6 kale stems, 2 inch leeks, 1 cup arugula, 1/2 bunch cilantro, 20 curry leaves, and 7-8 green chillies (or less), and all of the mixed soaked dals, along with 2 cups water. Add more water, if needed. The batter was not fermented. If you'd like to ferment it, add 1 tsp fenugreek seeds when blending, and let it ferment overnight. CHEELA: Add some red onions and baby bok choy to the batter. Pour it on the pan to make a Cheela!
notes: A recipe with BEANS (various dals), LEAFY GREENS (kale stems, arugula, baby bok choy), RAINBOW VEGGIES (red onion, leeks, ginger, green chillies), FRUIT (dried prunes), HERBS & SPICES (various).

beans_legumes: seven different daals (beans of our choice)

all_ingredients_flat: quinoa, seven different daals, methi dana (fenugreek seeds), water, bottle gourd, pumpkin, red onion, carrot, capsicum, beetroot, hing (asafoetida), black pepper, ginger, sweetener (dates | maple syrup), green chillies, pink salt, curry leaves, ENO, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, sesame seeds, crushed peanuts
instructions:
BATTER:
1 cup quinoa, 1 cup of seven different daals (beans of our choice), 1/2 tsp methi dana (fenugreek seeds) — soak overnight, rinse well, add 3 tsp water, grind it & keep for 6 to 8 hours for fermentation.
Prepare 1.5 cups of grated mixed veggies of your choice. I used bottle gourd, pumpkin, red onion, carrot, capsicum, beetroot. Squeeze the juice out of grated veggies with hands to make them less watery — use this juice as a vegetable broth for another recipe.
Mix grated mixed vegetables with fermented batter. Add 1/4 tsp hing (asafoetida), 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 inch ginger (grated), 1/2 tsp sweetener (dates | maple syrup), some green chillies (to taste), 1/4 tsp pink salt (to taste), a few drops of lemon juice, 3-4 curry leaves (minced). Finally add 1 tsp ENO just before cooking the batter.
ROASTED MASALA:
Dry roast mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, sesame seeds and some crushed peanuts.
Divide the batter into three equal portions.
UTHAPAM STYLE HANDVO: Pour one portion of batter on non-stick pan. Prepare like uthapam. Garnish with roasted masala. Cook for 5 to 8 minutes on slow flame, covered with a lid. Then flip it over and cook for another 5 to 8 minutes.
AIR FRIED HANDVO: Air fry the second portion of batter for 15 mins each side at 180 C.
serving_suggestion: Enjoy with Mint Chutney, Amla Chutney & plant-based yogurt!
notes: Use this juice as a vegetable broth for another recipe.

herbs_spices: 1 tsp baking soda or ENO fruit salt

all_ingredients_flat: brown rice (coarsely powdered), chana dal, moong dal, toor dal (coarsely powdered), minced garlic, turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, Garam Masala, white sesame seeds, grated ginger, ground green chillies, ground peanuts (coarsely powdered) - optional, salt, baking soda or ENO fruit salt, soy yogurt, shredded zucchini (or opo squash), shredded beetroot, water, mustard seeds, sesame seeds, asafetida (hing), curry leaves, lemon juice
instructions:
(1) Coarsely powder brown rice & all the dals. (2) Blend green chillies (according to your preference), garlic and ginger. (3) Add various spices, soy yogurt, ginger/garlic/green chilli paste and add warm water to make a thick batter. (4) Add sesame seeds and peanut powder. Mix well without any lumps. (5) Set aside for 5-6 hrs for fermentation. (6) After the batter has fermented, add grated zucchini, beets, salt [to taste], lemon juice, and baking soda (or ENO salt).

TEMPERING (Preparation):
Dry roast all the ingredients. Add water at the end.

TEMPERING (Cooking):
BAKE: Transfer the batter into silicon muffin pan. Add tempering (made mustard seeds, sesame seeds, curry leaves, ...) as topping on the batter. Bake at 350 F for almost 45-60 mins. Check after 35 mins (by inserting a toothpick). If not done then let bake for another 10-20 mins.
serving_suggestion: Enjoy with Homemade Ketchup.
notes: A recipe with WHOLE GRAINS (brown rice), BEANS (chana dal, moong dal, toor dal, soy yogurt), RAINBOW VEGGIES (zucchini, beetroot), NUTS & SEEDS (sesame seeds, peanuts), HERBS & & SPICES (various).

creator: Sudisha Bhola Arora
all_ingredients_flat: besan (chickpea flour), warm water, cilantro, minced onion, salt, Chaat Masala, jeera (cumin powder), haldi (turmeric powder), firm tofu, Garam Masala
instructions:
Besan Cheela Batter: Mix besan (chickpea flour) with warm water to make a smooth thick batter. Add cilantro, minced onion, salt (to taste), Chaat Masala, jeera (cumin powder) & haldi (turmeric powder). Mix well.
Pour Besan Cheela Batter into waffle iron. Then place a slice of firm tofu and cover it with more batter on top. Alternately, we may dip tofu slices in batter and place them in waffle iron.

creator: Kusum Dhairyawan
all_ingredients_flat: cilantro leaves, mint leaves, curry leaves, green chillies, ginger, garlic cloves, toasted sesame seeds, roasted peanuts, lemon juice, green mango, amla, date, water, quinoa, chana dal, spinach, amaranth leaves, turmeric powder, black pepper, hing (asafetida), lime
instructions:
GREEN CHUTNEY:
Blend together 1/2 bunch cilantro leaves, 1 handful of mint leaves, 7-8 curry leaves, 2-3 green chillies, 1 inch piece ginger, 2-3 garlic cloves (optional), 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds, 1 Tbsp roasted peanuts, 1/2 lemon juice (or sour fruit like green mango or amla), 1 date for sweetness & some water into a smooth chutney.

BATTER:
Soak 1/2 cup quinoa & 1/2 cup chana dal in water for 5-6 hours.
Add 2 small green chillies, 8-9 curry leaves & 1 inch ginger. Grind to a paste. Let the batter sit overnight or 7-8 hours for fermentation.
Add these to the batter & mix thoroughly: a handful of spinach (finely chopped), a handful of amaranth leaves (finely chopped), a handful of cilantro (finely chopped), 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, a pinch of black pepper, a pinch of hing (asafetida), juice of 1/2 lime.

STEAMING:
Cut parchment paper (or wet cheese cloth) to the shape of a big thali (steel plate). Place it on the steel plate, then pour batter into the plate.
Add 2 cups of water in one big wok. Place a ring inside the wok. Let the water boil. Once water starts to boil, place the steel plate with batter over the ring (without submerging the batter in water). Cover the wok with the lid. Let the batter steam at medium high heat for 20 mins until we see the batter leaving the side of the plate.
Remove the lid. Let the dhokla plate cool completely. Cut into squares for serving. Remove parchment paper.
serving_suggestion: Garnish with more cilantro leaves. Serve with Green Chutney.
notes: This recipe includes sub-recipes for Green Chutney and Batter. Batter requires overnight or 7-8 hours for fermentation.

all_ingredients_flat: chana dal, hing (asafoetida), beetroot, onion, carrot, green beans, ginger, green chili, black pepper, garlic powder, raw mango powder, mustard seeds, curry leaves, white sesame seeds, date paste, lemon juice, mint leaves, raisins, dried berries, Green Chutney
instructions:
SOAK & FERMENT: Soak 1/2 cup chana dal for 4 hours. Drain water, grind it with 1/4 tsp hing (asafoetida). Add water if required but not more than 1 or 2 tsp. Keep it for 8 to 10 hours for fermentation.
BATTER: Add 1/2 cup of finely chopped Rainbow Vegetables of your choice: beetroot, onion, carrot, green beans. Add finely minced ginger (a small piece), 1/2 green chili, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp anchor (raw mango powder). Mix all the ingredients.
STEAM: Transfer the batter to a container: small bowls. Steam for 20 to 25 minutes.
TADKA: Dry roast 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 4-5 five curry leaves, 3 to 4 green chillis, 1/4 tsp white sesame seeds, 1/2 tsp date paste, 1/2 tsp lemon juice. Boil for 2 to 3 minutes.
SERVE: Remove dhokla from bowls. Pour TADKA on dhokla. Garnish with mint leaves, raisins, some dried berries. Serve with Green Chutney.

text:
Recipe: Dhokla
Creator: Mrs N K Manku
Category: Chaat
Ingredients: chana dal, hing (asafoetida), beetroot, onion, carrot, green beans, ginger, green chili, black pepper, garlic powder, raw mango powder, mustard seeds, curry leaves, white sesame seeds, date paste, lemon juice, mint leaves, raisins, dried berries, Green Chutney
Cooking methods: no-cook, blend, steam, roast, boil
Instructions: SOAK & FERMENT: Soak 1/2 cup chana dal for 4 hours. Drain water, grind it with 1/4 tsp hing (asafoetida). Add water if required but not more than 1 or 2 tsp. Keep it for 8 to 10 hours for fermentation.
BATTER: Add 1/2 cup of finely chopped Rainbow Vegetables of your choice: beetroot, onion, carrot, green beans. Add finely minced ginger (a small piece), 1/2 green chili, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp anchor (raw mango powder). Mix all the ingredients.
STEAM: Transfer the batter to a container: small bowls. Steam for 20 to 25 minutes.
TADKA: Dry roast 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 4-5 five curry leaves, 3 to 4 green chillis, 1/4 tsp white sesame seeds, 1/2 tsp date paste, 1/2 tsp lemon juice. Boil for 2 to 3 minutes.
SERVE: Remove dhokla from bowls. Pour TADKA on dhokla. Garnish with mint leaves, raisins, some dried berries. Serve with Green Chutney.
Notes: Green Chutney

creator: Nivedita Dogra Dubey
all_ingredients_flat: yellow mung dal, urad dal, soy yogurt, onion, fruit salt, ENO, roasted cumin powder, black salt, red chili powder, Tamarind Chutney
instructions:
BATTER: Soak yellow mung dal for a couple of hours. Then grind it. Whisk the batter for few minutes till fluffy. Then add 1/2 tsp fruit salt. I added ENO.
STEAM: Steam in idli stand for 12 to 15 minutes. We can check with tip of knife – It should come off clean when poked into the steaming vada.
HOT WATER SOAK: Dip the steamed vada in hot water for a few minutes, then drain. No need to squeeze out water. It doesn't soak much.
SERVE: Add plant-based yogurt. Garnish with roasted cumin powder, black salt (if using salt), red chili powder and Tamarind Chutney.
serving_suggestion: Add plant-based yogurt. Garnish with roasted cumin powder, black salt (if using salt), red chili powder and Tamarind Chutney.

creator: Kiran Sharma
all_ingredients_flat: sweet potatoes, paprika, 21 Seasoning Salute Blend, black pepper powder, dried parsley, Garlic Tahini, blackstrap molasses, chickpeas, sweet corn, pomegranate seeds
instructions:
PREP: (a) Preheat the oven to 420F. (b) Scrub the sweet potatoes clean. I left the peel on.
Cook sweet potatoes partially. I cooked them in a pressure cooker (opened 5 minutes after the first whistle). At this point, sweet potatoes were half cooked.
Chop the half cooked sweet potatoes into fries of any shape; wedges with thickness 1/2" to 3/4" are recommended.
Toss sweet potato wedges into a large bowl. Sprinkle some water and any seasonings of your choice. Mix well.
Place the seasoned wedges inside a baking tray lined with a Silicone Mat, making sure they do not touch.
Bake for 35-40 minutes. Turn them over after 20 minutes. Cook them until they turn golden brown and crispy.
Serve with Garlic Tahini, a drizzle of blackstrap molasses along with toasted chickpeas, corn, and pomegranate seeds.
serving_suggestion: Serve with Garlic Tahini, a drizzle of blackstrap molasses along with toasted chickpeas, corn, and pomegranate seeds.
notes: Sprinkling some water on sweet potato wedges, helps the seasoning to adhere and avoid burning.

instructions:
VADA:
+ SOAK: Soak urad dal for 6-8 hours.
+ GRIND: Grind soaked urad dal into a smooth batter using some water. Make a thick batter, not runny. Wet grinder works best; use ice cold water. Add a little bit of ginger and Green Chilli Paste, salt (to taste) and a little bit of baking soda. Let the batter rest for 15 mins.
+ BAKE: Preheat oven to 425 F. Pour the batter into baking trays for donuts. Bake for 10-12 mins, checking in between.
DAHI:
+ DRY TADKA: Dry sauté some cumin seeds, mustard seeds, urad dal, curry leaves; then add grated ginger & thinly diced green chillis.
+
serving_suggestion: Pour some cold Dahi into a serving bowl. Add baked Vadas and let them soak for 15-20 minutes. Garnish with broccoli sprouts and grated carrot.

instructions:
MOONG DAL PAKODI: Soak 1/2 cup yellow moong daal in water for 4 hours. Drain the water, then grind with 1 to 2 tsp water and 1/4 tsp asafetida (hing). Add 1 tsp ENO and 1 tsp water. Mix well to form a batter. Transfer the batter into idli moulds. Steam for ten minutes. Then soak them in regular water (at room temperature) for 10 minutes.
PAPDI: Make a tight dough with whole wheat flour and water. Made a large-sized roti. Using a cookie cutter or the top of a small bottle, make small-sized thin rotis. Cook them on low flame so that they become crispy.

notes: This is a Whole Food Plant-Based recipe. Sub-recipes mentioned are Green Chutney, Amla Chutney, and Sonth (Sweet Tamarind Chutney). ENO is used as an ingredient.

instructions:
DRY TADKA: Combine coriander seeds, coriander powder, cumin powder, red chilli powder, fennel powder, Garam Masala powder and salt (if using). Mix well. Sauté for 2 minutes. Add a little bit of water to avoid over cooking.
DAL MIXTURE: Add soaked moong daal to Dry Tadka. Add 1/2 cup water, dry mango powder and Chaat Masala too. Mix well. Cook till moong daal is fully cooked. When dal mixture becomes dry, transfer it into another bowl and let it cool.
DOUGH: Put whole wheat flour in a bowl. Add salt (if using), baking powder, and carom seeds. Mix well. Add sufficient water, knead into a stiff dough. Cover the bowl with cloth and rest the dough for 20 minutes.
KACHORI: Divide the dough into equal portions and shape into balls. Press them slightly and roll out into small puris with the edges being thinner than the centre. Place some Dal Mixture in the centre, dampen the edges, bring them together and press to seal. Press slightly and roll into small puris ensuring that the filling is evenly spread.
serving_suggestion: Arrange kachoris on a serving plate. Serve them hot with Tamarind Chutney and Aaloo Sabji (potato curry).

instructions: For Green Chutney: Grind coriander leaves, mint leaves, green chillies, lemon juice, vinegar, and garlic cloves to make a coarse chutney. For Red Sauce: Grind tomato, green chilli, jalapeño, dried red chillies, red bell pepper, yellow bell pepper, coriander leaves, lemon juice, vinegar, and walnuts to make a coarse chutney. For Shor Nakhod: Pressure cook 1 cup garbanzo beans (chickpeas; soaked overnight) with turmeric, 1 inch cinnamon stick & Himalayan salt. Open the pressure cooker 20 minutes after the first whistle on low heat. Optionally mash some of the chickpeas to make them thicker (less watery). Cut Yukon potatoes into 1 inch pieces. Add them to boiling water with turmeric powder & some mint leaves. Cook at low flame for 5-7 minutes. Assembly: Serve a few Tbsp of garbanzo beans to a bowl. Add some cooked potatoes. Then garnish with Green Chutney & Red Chutney.

creator: Kiran Sharma
all_ingredients_flat: Tofu, Black pepper powder, Red chilli powder, Turmeric powder, Garam Masala, Cumin powder, Coriander powder, Lemon, Chickpea flour (besan), Red Ragi Upma Rava, Brown Rice Powder, Baking soda, Sumac powder, Garlic powder, Onion powder, Water, Soy yogurt, Carom seeds (ajwain), Himalayan salt
instructions:
For Masala Marinade: Mix black pepper powder (1/2 tsp), red chilli powder (1 tsp), turmeric powder (1/4 tsp), garam masala (1 tsp), cumin powder (1 tsp), coriander powder (1/2 tsp), and freshly squeezed lemon (1 Tbsp) into a thick paste.
For Chickpea Batter: Mix chickpea flour (besan) (1/3 cup), Red Ragi Upma Rava (1.5 Tbsp, Brown Rice Powder will do too), black pepper powder (1 tsp), red chilli powder (1.5 tsp), turmeric powder (1/4 tsp), garam masala powder (1.5 tsp), cumin powder (1 tsp), baking soda (a pinch), sumac powder (1 tsp), garlic powder (1 tsp), onion powder (1 tsp), water or soy yogurt (1/4 cup, adjust quantity if batter is thick, I used water), carom seeds (ajwain) (1/2 tsp), and optional Himalayan salt into a thick paste.
To make Tofu Pakoda: Take two 1/2 inch slices of tofu. Drain the water using Tofu Press. Wrap tofu in cheese cloth and place a heavy object on it for 3-4 hours. Make 2-3 criss cross cuts on tofu slices. Cover them generously with Masala Marinade. Set aside for 20-25 minutes for marination. Dip marinated tofu slices in Chickpea Batter. Apply the batter on both sides, covering the slices fully. Preheat the air fryer at 350 F. The air fryer container must be warm before we place Tofu Pakodas in it. Place Tofu Pakodas in the air fryer. Turn them over after 8 minutes. If the Pakodas is sticking to the bottom then cook for another minute before turning over. Cook for another 8-10 minutes. Turn them over. Pakodas should feel crisp to the touch. Let them sit for 5-10 minutes.
serving_suggestion: Enjoy with any chutneys of your choice!
notes: A recipe with WHOLE GRAINS (Red Ragi Upma Rava | Brown Rice Powder), BEANS (tofu, chickpea flour), LIME-LEMON-VINEGAR (lemon), HERBS & SPICES (various). Sub-recipes: Masala Marinade, Chickpea Batter.

creator: Sudisha Bhola Arora
all_ingredients_flat: besan (chickpea flour), warm water, cilantro, minced onion, salt, Chaat Masala, jeera (cumin powder), haldi (turmeric powder), firm tofu, Garam Masala
instructions:
Besan Cheela Batter: Mix besan (chickpea flour) with warm water to make a smooth thick batter. Add cilantro, minced onion, salt (to taste), Chaat Masala, jeera (cumin powder) & haldi (turmeric powder). Mix well.

instructions:

Cook the potatoes partially. I cooked them in a pressure cooker (opened 5 minutes after the first whistle). At this point, potatoes were half cooked.
Chop the half cooked potatoes into fries of any shape; wedges with thickness 1/2" to 3/4" are recommended.
Toss potato wedges into a large bowl. Sprinkle some water and any seasonings of your choice. Mix well.
Place the seasoned wedges inside a baking tray lined with a Silicone Mat, making sure they do not touch.
Bake for 35-40 minutes. Turn them over after 20 minutes. Cook them until they turn golden brown and crispy.
Serve with Garlic Tahini!

all_ingredients_flat: millet flour, rag, finger millet, bajra, pearl millet, jowar, sorghum, besan, chickpea flour, flax, oats, chia seeds, hemp heart, baking powder, baking soda, water, ACV, Apple Cider Vinegar, whole psyllium husks, isabgol, dates, Italian herb mix, Jeera, cumin seeds, crushed walnuts, nuts, seeds, minced garlic, jalapenos
instructions:
Gluten-Free Bread is dense in texture. Takes 15 minutes for prep and then 2 hours to bake. Lasts 1 week in my fridge.
*   BATTER: Mix water, vinegar and isabgol (psyllium husks). Set aside for 5 mins. Mix the rest of the ingredients (dry ingredients) in a bowl thoroughly. Then add the isabgol, water & vinegar mix.
*   BAKING PAN: For oil-free preparation, use a non-stick baking pan. I prefer to use a glass baking pan with 1/4 tsp oil to coat the entire baking dish. I use a brush to ensure even coating.
*   BAKING: Pour the batter into the baking pan. I score the middle and lower the height so that after baking, the top is more even in height. Set oven on bake (no convection) at 325 F. Bake for 120 mins. You may need to experiment with the settings depending on oven.
*   SLICING & TOASTING: Let cool before slicing. The bread may be a little damp when we slice it, but it comes out right upon toasting. I toast each slice for about 9 minutes at 425 F.

all_ingredients_flat: nutritional yeast, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, cashews, turmeric powder, pepper powder, red chili powder, garlic cloves, roasted red pepper, dates, smoked paprika, kale, Apple Cider Vinegar, mustard seed powder
instructions: SPICE RUB: Grind these together: 1/2 cup nutritional yeast, 1/2 pumpkin seeds, soaked in water for 10-15 minutes [alternatives: sunflower seeds or cashews], 1 tsp turmeric powder, 1/4 tsp pepper powder, 1 Tbsp red chili powder, 4-5 garlic cloves, 1 big roasted red pepper, 4-5 dates, 1-2 tsp smoked paprika. KALE CHIPS: Wash 2 bunches of kale. Remove the ribs. Break kale leaves with hands and massage them with 1-2 tsp ACV (Apple Cider Vinegar). Then coat them with Spice Rub and bake them at 325 F for 30-35 minutes, checking in between. Then sprinkle 1 tsp freshly ground mustard seed powder on kale chips.
notes: TIPS: (1) To make them crispy, apply less Spice Rub. (2) Adjust the level of spiciness with less or more chili powder.

creator: Kiran Sharma
all_ingredients_flat: White peas, Onions, Ginger Garlic Paste, Green chili, Himalayan salt, Turmeric powder, Red chilli powder, Garam Masala Powder, Hing (asafetida), Tamarind paste, Date sugar, Cilantro, Pomegranate, Green Chutney
instructions:
WHITE PEAS: Soak white peas overnight. Pressure cook them in the Instant Pot for 15-20 minutes. Mash 3-4 Tbsp cooked peas in a bowl & set them aside. I drained the peas out and used the Instant Pot for sautéing the masala as well.
MASALA: Set Instant Pot to sauté mode. Dry sauté onions & green chili until onion turn translucent. I add some water to keep the onions from sticking to the bottom. Then add Ginger Garlic paste & cook for 1 minute. Then add hing, red chili powder, turmeric powder, Garam Masala Powder & 1 Tbsp water. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Combine cooked peas, mashed peas, date sugar, tamarind paste & Himalayan salt [optional, to taste].Adjust the quantity of water. Bring to a boil, then cook for 7-10 minutes on low flame. Do a taste check & add more Garam Masala powder or red chili powder, if needed.
Garnish with chopped cilantro, pomegranate & Green Chutney!
serving_suggestion: Garnish with chopped cilantro, pomegranate & Green Chutney!
notes: A recipe with BEANS (white peas), RAINBOW VEGGIES (onion), FRUITS (pomegranate), SWEETENER (date sugar), HERBS & SPICES (various). Himalayan salt [optional, to taste]. Adjust quantity of water. Add more Garam Masala powder or red chili powder, if needed. Add some water to keep onions from sticking to the bottom.

rainbow_veggies: bell peppers (mentioned in instructions, not in ingredient list)

all_ingredients_flat: potatoes, beetroot, frozen veggies mix, carrots, beans, corn, green peas, green chillies, ginger piece, red bell pepper, cilantro, mint leaves, Ginger Garlic Paste, turmeric powder, black pepper powder, red chili powder, Chaat Masala, amchur powder, salt, chia seeds, hempseed, Ezekiel 4:9 bread, sooji (upma rava or farina), whole wheat flour, water, bell peppers
instructions:
Veggies: In a thick bottom pan, cook frozen veggies on medium heat for 5-10 mins. Then add beetroot, bell peppers, green chillies, ginger and all the spices except Ginger Garlic Paste. Cook for 3-4 minutes. Then add boiled potato pieces. Mix well & mash with a potato masher or a thick spoon. Now add Ginger Garlic Paste. Mix well and cook for a minute. Add greens, cilantro and mint. Mix well and switch off the stove. Don't cook after adding greens. Let mixture cool before making patties.
Bread Crumbs [optional]: Toast bread slices to make them hard. Grind them along with chia seeds and hemp seeds. Mix sooji rava.
Make patties: Make round patties using the vegetable mix. If using bread crumbs, dip the patty in the water and flour mixture, then dip in bread crumbs mix to evenly coat the patty with bread crumbs. Freeze these patties for 1 hour before cooking them.
Cook patties: Cook both sides for 5 minutes each on medium heat in a pan. Then air fry for 4 minutes on each side.
serving_suggestion: Garnish like microgreens, red onions, tomatoes & homemade ketchup.
notes: Bread Crumbs [optional]. A recipe with WHOLE GRAINS (corn, Ezekiel 4:9 bread), BEANS (green peas, Ezekiel 4:9 bread), TUBERS (potato), RAINBOW VEGGIES (beetroot, carrot, bell pepper...), NUTS & SEEDS (chia seeds, hempseed), HERBS & SPICES (various).

instructions:
Steps for 12-15 Tikkis
* Cook 1 cup whole red lentils with 1:1 water in Instant Pot for 12 minutes. Let it cool down.
* Chop 1 small onion, 1/2 red pepper, 1/2 green pepper. Sauté them until onion is translucent. Add grated ginger & 3-4 garlic cloves. Continue to sauté for 1-2 minutes. Let this mixture cool down.
* Mix together cooked lentils & sautéed veggies in a food processor. Add 1 tbsp flaxseed meal, 1 tbsp sesame seeds, salt as per taste, 1/2 to 1 tsp red chili powder (to taste), 1 tsp coriander cumin powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, 1/4 tsp black pepper powder, 1 cup chopped cilantro, 1 tsp onion powder and 4 tbsp 'kala chana besan'. Mix until combined (not like paste).
* Air fry at 350F for 10 minutes. Flip and air fry for another 5 minutes until golden brown. Or bake at 350F for 12 minutes; flip and bake for another 10 minutes. Serve with cilantro chutney!
serving_suggestion: Serve with cilantro chutney!
notes: Yields 12-15 Tikkis.

creator: Aishwarya Parasuram
all_ingredients_flat: garlic cloves, green chili, cumin seeds, water, jowar flour, sorghum flour
instructions:
SPICE PASTE: Blend together 4 garlic cloves, 2 green chili, 1 Tbsp cumin seeds and a little water till it forms a paste.
JOWAR MUTTIGE:
+ Add 0.5 cup boiling water to 1 cup jowar flour (sorghum flour) and knead into dough. While kneading, add room temperature water 1 Tbsp at a time as needed.
+ Take some dough and flatten into a slightly thick roti using your palm and a flat surface (similar to making jowar roti).
+ Put roti on heated pan, glaze the top of roti with water as it cooks. After one side is cooked, flip and repeat till roti is properly cooked on both sides.
+ Remove from pan. Spread spice paste on one surface. Immediately crush it back into a ball while it is still hot.
notes: A recipe with WHOLE GRAINS (sorghum flour), HERBS & SPICES (garlic cloves, green chili, cumin seeds).

creator: Kiran Sharma
all_ingredients_flat: Brown Rice Paper, Water, Cauliflower, Peas, Potato, various Herbs & Spices, Ezekiel Bread Crumbs, Steel Cut Oats Bread Crumbs
instructions:
BROWN RICE PAPER: Dip brown rice paper in water for a few seconds. Leaving it in for long will make it a wet mush. Then place the wet paper on a rolling platform [I used a steel rolling platform]. Use a knife to slice the paper into 2 halves.
FILLING: Place a spoonful of sabzi on one end of the paper leaving some room to roll the paper with the sabzi (see pic). Gently place the roll in the bread crumbs plate and cover it with the bread crumbs.
BAKE: Place the rolls on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Heat the oven at 350 F and bake the rolls for 25-30 minutes or until the outside turns crunchy.
serving_suggestion: Enjoy with any chutneys of your choice.
notes: Brown Rice Paper - 4 [will make 8 Bread Rolls]. Cauliflower Peas & Potato Sabzi [described in its own recipe card]. Ezekiel Bread Crumbs or Steel Cut Oats Bread Crumbs [described in their own recipe cards]. [I used a steel rolling platform]. (see pic).

creator: Kusum Dhairyawan
all_ingredients_flat: Besan (chickpea flour), water, tamarind paste, green chili, ginger, garlic, cilantro, turmeric, hing (asafoetida), ajwain (carom seeds), salt, date sugar, ENO, collard leaves
instructions:
Combine these together, along with water to make a thick batter for coating collard leaves:
- Besan (chickpea flour) - 3 cups
- 1 Tbsp tamarind paste (not from concentrate) - homemade by soaking tamarind and squeezing the pulp
- 1 green chili (finely chopped), 1/2 inch ginger (finely grated), 2 cloves of garlic (grated, optional), a handful of cilantro (finely chopped)
- Spices - turmeric, a pinch of hing (asafoetida), 1/2 tsp ajwain (carom seeds), salt (optional, to taste) and 1 tsp date sugar, and a pinch of ENO

PATRA
- Wash and dry collard leaves. Then remove the stems (the central ribs); use stems in a separate recipe.
- Lay down a leaf on a flat surface. Coat it with thick batter from top to bottom. Then lay another leaf over the first leaf (coated with batter). Coat the second leaf with batter. Optionally, we may lay down a third leaf on top of the second leaf and coat it with batter - it depends on the size of leaves. Then roll them together like a spring roll.
- Steam the rolls in a steamer for 30 mins. Insert a knife to check - if it comes out clean, that means the rolls are cooked thoroughly.
- Let it cool completely before cutting into slices as shown in pic.
- Serve with Green Chutney or Sweet Chutney.
serving_suggestion: Serve with Green Chutney or Sweet Chutney.
notes: Use stems in a separate recipe. Tamarind paste (not from concentrate) - homemade by soaking tamarind and squeezing the pulp. Garlic (grated, optional). Salt (optional, to taste). Recipe: Collard Greens Patra
Creator: Kusum Dhairyawan
Category: Patra
Ingredients: Besan (chickpea flour), water, tamarind paste, green chili, ginger, garlic, cilantro, turmeric, hing (asafoetida), ajwain (carom seeds), salt, date sugar, ENO, collard leaves
Cooking methods: steam
Instructions: Combine these together, along with water to make a thick batter for coating collard leaves:
- Besan (chickpea flour) - 3 cups
- 1 Tbsp tamarind paste (not from concentrate) - homemade by soaking tamarind and squeezing the pulp
- 1 green chili (finely chopped), 1/2 inch ginger (finely grated), 2 cloves of garlic (grated, optional), a handful of cilantro (finely chopped)
- Spices - turmeric, a pinch of hing (asafoetida), 1/2 tsp ajwain (carom seeds), salt (optional, to taste) and 1 tsp date sugar, and a pinch of ENO

PATRA
- Wash and dry collard leaves. Then remove the stems (the central ribs); use stems in a separate recipe.
- Lay down a leaf on a flat surface. Coat it with thick batter from top to bottom. Then lay another leaf over the first leaf (coated with batter). Coat the second leaf with batter. Optionally, we may lay down a third leaf on top of the second leaf and coat it with batter - it depends on the size of leaves. Then roll them together like a spring roll.
- Steam the rolls in a steamer for 30 mins. Insert a knife to check - if it comes out clean, that means the rolls are cooked thoroughly.
- Let it cool completely before cutting into slices as shown in pic.
- Serve with Green Chutney or Sweet Chutney.
Notes: Use stems in a separate recipe. Tamarind paste (not from concentrate) - homemade by soaking tamarind and squeezing the pulp. Garlic (grated, optional). Salt (optional, to taste). Optionally, we may lay down a third leaf on top of the second leaf and coat it with batter - it depends on the size of leaves.

text:
Ingredients:
1. Coriander seeds - 2 tbsp
2. Red chillies - 8 to 10
3. Cloves - 6
4. Cinnamon - 1.5 inch
5. Black cardamom - 1
6. Green cardamom - 3
7. Mace - 1
8. Star anise - 1
9. Black pepper - 8 to 10
10. Stone flower - 1/2 tbsp
11. Cumin seeds - 1 tsp
12. Fennel seeds - 1 tsp
13. Sesame seeds - 1/2 tbsp
14. Poppy seeds - 1/2 tbsp
15. Garlic - 3 to 4 cloves
16. Red onion - 1, evenly and thinly sliced
17. Ground ginger powder - 3/4 tsp
18. Red chilli powder - 1 to 1.5 tsp (Kashmiri for color)

Method:
1. Heat a pan. Add ingredients 1-10. Slow roast for 2 minutes or until slightly fragrant on low to medium heat to prevent burning.
2. Add cumin seeds + fennel seeds; roast slightly.
3. Add sesame + poppy seeds. Add garlic cloves and toast them until they turn a little dry and warm.
4. Set these aside to cool.
5. Toast the sliced onions in a pan for 10-12 minutes until dark brown, or dehydrate in an air fryer until crisp (Gurmeet used an air fryer).
6. After everything cools down, grind the spices (except onions and garlic) using a pulse setting. Add ginger powder + red chilli powder.
7. Add the onions and garlic. Pulse in intervals of 30-40 seconds.
8. Store in an airtight container.
Note: This recipe includes onion and garlic, making it more akin to a Misal Masala.

text:
Discussion on whether dry roasted quinoa can be cooked quickly with hot water (off-flame) for backpacking.
- One member suggests that quinoa needs time for water to soften it, and dry roasting followed by hot water might leave the core hard. Testing at home is recommended.
- Partially cooking and then drying it might work better.
- Toasted quinoa can be eaten as is for a nutty flavor in salads or cooked later. Toasting before cooking is a common practice.
- It is believed that if boiled and covered, it should cook in hot water off-flame.
- Bulgur wheat is suggested as an alternative that works well with just soaking (as in tabbouleh).
- Quinoa benefits from pre-soaking to dissolve the bitter exterior, but still needs to be cooked.

creator: Gurmeet, Padma WFPB
text:
Ingredients: Soy milk (Trader Joe's, Westlife, Eden Foods brands are mentioned), 1 tbsp saved soy yogurt culture (starter).
Method (Gurmeet's):
1. Heat soy milk in the microwave for 3 minutes. Stir, let it cool until warm to the touch.
2. Add 1 tbsp of saved culture and mix well.
3. Place in an Instant Pot on yogurt setting (typically 8 hours). Gurmeet sometimes keeps it out for a few more hours for a sourer taste.
Method (Padma's - no heating):
1. Just add 1 spoon of starter soy yogurt to soy milk, whisk thoroughly.
2. Keep it to proof for 9-10 hours until 'cuts' appear on top. Padma uses the proof setting on her oven or leaves it for up to 18 hours without issues.
Discussion points:
- Gurmeet found that without heating, the consistency was runny and watery.
- Optimal temperature for bacterial proliferation is ~40-50°C (100-120°F), suggesting heating might be necessary depending on ambient temperature.
- Keeping it too long in the Instant Pot (beyond 8 hours) can make it rancid for Gurmeet, but Padma has left it for 18 hours without issues.
- The starter can initially be from dairy yogurt, then subsequent batches use saved soy yogurt culture.

For tubers like potatoes and sweet potatoes, pressure cooking is a good option, but any WFPB compliant method is fine as long as they are consumed. recipe_name: Managing GI Issues with Raw vs. Cooked Foods
creator: Group Member, Gurmeet Singh Manku, Kusum WFPB
text:
A member experienced GI issues (gas and bloating) after increasing raw food intake. Their acupuncturist suggested eliminating raw foods and eating only cooked food. After trying this, GI issues drastically improved.
- Gurmeet Singh Manku suggests that eating cooked greens (e.g., steaming hard greens like kale and collards) can help consume more leafy greens, as cooking breaks down cell walls, releasing nutrients. He advocates for eating as many leafy greens as possible, whether raw or cooked, and trying different varieties.
- It's noted that the body sometimes needs time to adapt to increased fiber, and starting slow with small amounts of raw food might help.
- For further discussion on GI tract conditions, the WFPB Chit Chat group is recommended.

Ingredients: Whole urad dal, black peppercorns, hing (asafoetida), green chilli, ginger (chopped onions optional), ice cold water. For dahi flavoring: red chilli powder, garam masala powder, sumac, amchoor (dry mango powder), cumin powder, black salt. Method:
1. Soak urad dal overnight or for 6 hours.
2. Grind dal with black peppercorns, hing, green chilli, and ginger (and optional chopped onions) to a thick, fluffy batter. Use ice cold water while grinding to prevent the batter from heating up, which can result in hard wadas.
3. Ferment the batter overnight.
4. For baking: Preheat oven to 350°F.
5. Use a muffin tin lined with muffin cups (silicon muffin tin is ideal). Lightly brush some water on the muffin paper cups.
6. Pour the batter into the cups and bake for approximately 15 minutes or until a skewer comes out clean.
7. Let the wadas cool slightly, then gently remove them from the paper cups.
8. Soak the wadas in warm water for 5-7 minutes. Squeeze all the water out.
9. Add the wadas to dahi (plant-based yogurt).
10. To flavor the dahi: Add red chilli powder, garam masala powder, sumac, amchoor, cumin powder, and black salt.

creator: Uma Venkataraman WFPB
text: Soak 1.5 cups of almonds for about 2 hours until plumped. Blend with 4 cups of cold water (or ice/cold water combo) in a high-speed blender for 2 minutes. Strain the mixture, reserving the pulp for other recipes. This recipe uses only the almond milk. Pour the cold milk into a saucepan. Dissolve 1/2 Tbsp arrowroot powder and 1/2 Tbsp agar agar into a small amount of cold almond milk until completely incorporated, then mix into the entire batch of almond milk. Heat on medium heat until it's almost boiling, but do not let it boil over. Let the mixture cool to baby bath water temperature before adding a yogurt starter and setting it. Uma leaves it in an Instant Pot for 16 to 24 hours; 24 hours yields a very tart yogurt, great for kadhi. Other thickeners like 1/2 Tbsp corn starch and 1/2 tsp xanthan gum also work, but agar agar-arrowroot powder was preferred.

creator: Kusum WFPB
text: Kusum makes her chaat masala at home using roasted cumin seeds, roasted coriander seeds, a few dried red chilies, a couple of cloves, a few black peppercorns, black salt, amchoor (dry mango powder), lemon powder, dried mint leaves, and hing (asafoetida). creator: Gurmeet
text: Blend 2 ripe, peeled persimmons, 5 tsps cacao powder, 6 dates, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract (optional), and 2-3 tbs plant-based milk (Gurmeet used soy milk). Pour the mixture into small cups or bowls and refrigerate for 4 hours or more. Turn upside down onto plates and enjoy. Optional garnish with almond slivers or pista. A group member suggested silken tofu as a great substitute for persimmons if they are not in season.

creator: Leena Menon WFPB
text:
Ingredients:
- Potatoes
- Satvic cashew cheese (recipe below)
- Roasted bell pepper
- Brine: 1 tbsp black pepper, 0.25 cup soy sauce, 1 cup rice vinegar, 1 cup water

Method:
1. Cut potatoes in half and brine them overnight in the prepared brine solution.
2. The next day, boil the brined potatoes in the brine water, then drain.
3. Slice the potatoes and layer them in a pan.
4. Bake at 370°F for 25 minutes. Turn off the oven.
5. Top the potatoes with Satvic cashew cheese and roasted bell pepper.
6. Put back in the oven for 10 minutes.

Satvic Cashew Cheese:
- 1 cup cashews (soaked in hot water for 30 minutes)
- 1.5 cup boiled cauliflower
- 3/4 tsp salt
- 4 tbsp nutritional yeast
- 1 tbsp ACV (Apple Cider Vinegar)
- 1.5 cup water
Grind all Satvic cashew cheese ingredients together until smooth.

creator: Prathima WFPB
text: Dry roast mustard seeds, cumin seeds, onion, tomato, and raw banana. Add 1/2 cup water. Incorporate spices such as sambar powder, garam masala, salt, turmeric, or any other preferred spices. Garnish with coriander leaves and roasted peanut powder. This is a quick and easy recipe.

creator: Prathima WFPB
text: Combine besan (chickpea flour), soft silken tofu, kala namak (black salt), and chili powder. Blend these ingredients together without adding any water to create a thick mix. This mix can be used as a coating, for example, for air-fried bread pakoda stuffed with potato.

creator: Prathima WFPB
text:
Base Recipe:
- Raw grated potato (use a small grater), approximately 2-3 potatoes
- Chopped Coriander leaves, 3-4 tsp
- Chopped Green chili, 1-2
- Grated coconut (part of the original recipe, but Prathima skipped it), 2 tsp
- Roasted groundnut crushed/powder, 3-4 tbsp
- Salt, as per taste
- Cumin seeds, 1 tsp
- Chili powder, optional

Method:
Mix all ingredients together. Tap the mixture onto a hot iron tawa (griddle). Cook on a low flame with a closed lid on both sides until done. The grated potatoes will bind together without releasing excessive water. Other grated vegetables and greens can be added, but potatoes should remain the primary ingredient.

creator: Leena Menon WFPB
text: For a WFPB BBQ skewer marinade, use balsamic vinegar, water, garlic powder, nutritional yeast, a little almond flour (to thicken), cayenne pepper, paprika, and white and black pepper. These spices and liquids can be used to marinate vegetables and tofu for grilling.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
This kheer can be made using leftover carrot juicer residue or fresh grated carrots. 
Ingredients:
1. Makhana (fox nuts), soaked in warm soy milk for 20-30 minutes.
2. Grated carrots.
3. Soy milk (for soaking makhana and cooking the kheer).
4. Cardamom powder.
5. Hemp hearts.
6. Date sugar.
7. Dates (for adding to the kheer and garnishing).
8. Cashews (for garnishing).
9. Soaked and partially cooked chana daal (optional, but suggested for improved taste).

Method:
Cook grated carrots, soy milk, cardamom powder, hemp hearts, date sugar, and dates for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally until the kheer thickens. Then, add the soaked makhana and cook for another 10 minutes. Garnish with dates and cashews.

creator: Divya CMU
text:
1. Steam desired vegetables (e.g., carrots, corn, beans, spinach, zucchini, brussel sprouts, garlic cloves) separately.
2. Keep other vegetables like mushrooms and capsicum aside, which will not be steamed.
3. In a pan, sauté finely chopped tomato, garlic, and ginger. Cool and grind into a paste.
4. Add the purée back to the pan, add the non-steamed vegetables, and coconut milk. Sauté for a while.
5. Add masalas such as cumin, turmeric, lemongrass, pepper, and salt. Then add the steamed vegetables.
6. Cook well and enjoy with brown rice or quinoa.

*Note: The group generally discourages the use of coconut in WFPB recipes. Refer to the 'Coconut Substitutes' entry for alternatives.*

creator: Prathima WFPB
text:
Dough:
- 1 cup whole wheat flour
- 1 cup almond flour
- 1/2 tsp baking powder
- Salt
- 1 cup water
Knead ingredients into a dough and let it rest for 15-30 minutes.

Cashew Butter:
- 1 cup cashews (made into butter)

Stuffing:
- Chopped nuts and seeds
- Black raisins
- Dried pineapple pieces
- Dates pieces
- Dates paste
- Cardamom powder
- Kesar (saffron), etc.

Method:
1. Roll out the dough. Spread cashew butter on it, fold, and repeat this process 5-6 times.
2. Place the rolled dough in the freezer for 20 minutes.
3. After freezing, roll it out again a couple of times, folding it with cashew butter in between.
4. Finally, roll it into a thick chapati dough consistency.
5. Place the sweet stuffing between two round rolled dough pieces.
6. Bake in an air fryer for 30 minutes at below 180°C, turning halfway through. The dough can also be used for pies and puffs.

creator: Prathima WFPB

creator: Gurmeet
text:
Ingredients:
- Tamarind: 1/2 cup, soaked in 1 cup water, pulp separated
- Dates: 5-6 Medjool dates
- Chili powder: 1 tsp or to taste
- Cumin powder: 2 tsp
- Coriander powder: 1.5 tsp
- Garam masala powder: 2 tsp or adjust as per taste
- Date sugar: 2 tsp or adjust as per taste

Method:
1. Add some water to the tamarind pulp and bring it to a boil.
2. Lower the heat and let it cook for 5-7 minutes until the mixture thickens.
3. Add the dates and continue cooking for another 6 minutes. Break down the dates with a spoon to integrate them into the chutney. (Gurmeet prefers a thick chutney with some date pieces and does not strain them out).
4. Add the masalas. Adjust masalas and thickness according to personal preference.
5. Enjoy!

creator: Gurmeet
text:
Ingredients:
- Tamarind: 1/4 cup, soaked in 1 cup water, pulp squeezed to extract liquid
- Black chana leftover water: 1/2 cup (optional)
- Beetroot leftover water: 1/4 cup (optional)
- Mustard seeds: 1/2 tsp
- Cumin seeds: 1/2 tsp
- Asafoetida: a pinch
- Curry leaves: 2 sprigs
- Green chili: 3
- Tomato: 1, cubed
- Frozen cranberries: 5-6
- Garlic: 1 clove, chopped
- Rasam powder: 1 tbsp or to taste
- Cilantro: for garnish

Method:
1. Dry temper the mustard and cumin seeds.
2. Add green chilies, asafoetida, and curry leaves.
3. Add the tomatoes, cranberries, and tamarind water. Bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes until the tomatoes soften slightly.
4. Add the black chana water and beetroot water (if using), along with rasam powder, cilantro, and garlic. Cook for another 5-7 minutes.
5. Enjoy! (Note: Black chana and beetroot water are optional additions if available).

creator: Group Member
text: Slit jalapeños and partially deseed them. Boil potatoes, mash them, and add salt, chili powder, turmeric, cumin, and coriander powder to taste. Stuff the jalapeños with this potato mixture. Air fry at 350°F for 20 minutes.

creator: Group Member
text:
Gatta:
Combine besan (chickpea flour), salt, ajwain (carom seeds), red chili powder, and a pinch of salt. Add half soy yogurt and half water to make a dough that is a bit firmer than roti dough. Roll the dough into finger-thick sticks, boil until cooked, then cut into desired shapes.

Curry:
Prepare a tadka with mustard seeds, curry patta, and green chilies. Add a mix of sour yogurt and the boiled gatta water (from cooking the gatta). Keep stirring until it boils, then simmer until the yogurt is cooked. Add the gatta pieces and simmer for a few more minutes. Garnish with coriander leaves.

Variations for Curry:
1. Use onion, garlic, and tomato paste.
2. Use tomato paste with or without yogurt.
3. Prepare as a regular yogurt kadhi.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
Ingredients:
- 4 tbsp coriander seeds / dhaniya seeds
- 2 tbsp cumin seeds / jeera
- 2 bay leaf / tej patta
- 10 cloves / lavang
- 2 cardamom / elachi
- 2 inch cinnamon stick / dalchini
- 1 tbsp pepper / kali mirch
- ¾ tbsp saunf / fennel seeds
- 10 dried kashmiri red chili / lal mirch
- 1 tsp turmeric powder / haldi
- 1 tbsp dry mango powder / aamchur powder
- 1.5 star anise
- 1/2 tsp dry ginger powder
- 1.5 black cardamom / junglee velchi
- 1 tbsp red chili powder
- 1 tsp turmeric

Method (Dry Roast):
1. Start by dry roasting the star anise until a floral aroma arises. Remove from the pan.
2. Next, add the coriander and cumin seeds. Roast and remove from the pan.
3. Add the rest of the whole spices (excluding the powders). Roast and set aside to cool.
4. Once cooled, blend all the roasted spices into a fine powder. Add the turmeric, dry mango powder, red chili powder, and the second turmeric measurement to this blend.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
This is a quick smoothie recipe, typically made with banana, but also works well with apples.

Ingredients (for 2 people):
- 2 tbsp hemp hearts
- 1/4 cup water (for soaking hemp hearts)
- 2 Medjool dates
- 1 elachi (cardamom)
- 1/2 an apple (or banana)
- 2 tbsp millet powder
- 3/4 cup water (for millet slurry)
- Soaked basil seeds (for topping, optional)

Method:
1. Soak 2 tbsp hemp hearts in 1/4 cup water in a blender jar for 5-7 minutes.
2. Blend the soaked hemp hearts to make milk.
3. Add 2 Medjool dates, 1 elachi, and 1/2 an apple (or banana) to the jar. Blend again.
4. In a separate pot, make a slurry of 2 tbsp millet powder in 3/4 cup water. Cook this until it thickens.
5. Let the cooked millet cool, then add it to the blender jar with the other ingredients. Blend until smooth.
6. Top with soaked basil seeds if desired.

text: Shalini shares extensive tips for WFPB meal prep and cooking while traveling. She chops and freezes celery, noting it cooks better this way. For travel, she cooks and freezes food, then packs it in hard coolers with frozen water bottles. This lasts 2-4 days. text: An accidental discovery revealed that adding psyllium husk (even a small amount like 1/3 cup) to a curry can cause it to soak up a lot of water and become a slimy, pudding-like consistency. creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text:
Coconuts are discouraged in WFPB guidelines due to their saturated fat content. Group members shared several substitutes:
- **Silken Tofu:** Sharmila Vedam suggests grinding silken tofu with 1-2 tbsp of coconut (for flavor) to achieve desired consistency for South Indian gravies.
- **Roasted Daliya:** Padma grinds a tiny amount of coconut for flavor with roasted daliya to mimic coconut-based gravy texture.
- **Fig Leaves:** Uma Venkataraman WFPB discovered that fig leaves have a hint of young coconut flavor and used them to wrap food for steaming or in desserts.
- **Celery (plus hemp or cashews):** Ambika uses celery as a substitute in koottu, chutneys, and pachadis. She notes that for sambar, coconut isn't necessary if fresh masala is made.
- **Soaked Raw Peanuts:** Ambika also suggests soaked raw peanuts for South Indian 'morekuzhambu'. She advises slowly reducing coconut and substituting with alternatives until the right taste is achieved, often masking substitute flavors with other seeds while blending.
External resources for coconut substitutes in Plant Based Desi Facebook group were also shared.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku clarified that organic noodles can be used if they are made from whole grains, not polished grains. Examples of compliant noodles include buckwheat noodles (soba), whole wheat noodles, or brown rice noodles. Non-compliant noodles to avoid are glass noodles (made from starch extracts) and typical rice noodles (made from polished white rice). The tip is to always check the ingredient list for whole grains versus polished grains or starch extracts.

text: Gurmeet Singh Manku provided two methods for making oil-free idli: 1. Using Silicone Idli Liners (available on Amazon and other retailers). 2. The 'Cloth Technique': cutting cotton cloth into a circular shape with a hole in the center to easily remove idli from the maker. Commercially sold cotton/muslin products for idli making are also available.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku shared a link to a long list of SOS-Free (without Salt, Oil & Sugar) WFPB products maintained by the NHA (National Health Association), USA: https://www.healthscience.org/health-science/sos-free-products/. The NHA has advocated the SOS-Free WFPB lifestyle since 1948.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Ingredients: 1 small brinjal (sliced into small pieces). Batter: 2 Tbsp besan (chickpea flour), 0.5 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp amchoor, 1 tsp Pancha Phoron spice mix (ground), 1 tsp crushed garlic, 1 tsp dried kasoori methi, a pinch of ajwain (carom seeds, rubbed between fingers), 2 tsp chopped cilantro (coriander leaves). Optional: minced green chili or chili flakes. Method: 1. Mix batter ingredients, adding water 1 tsp at a time to form a batter that is neither too hard nor too runny. 2. Coat brinjal slices with the batter on all sides. 3. Air fry for 10 minutes per side at 180°C. 4. Serve with green chutney, date chutney, lemon, and favorite spice mixes (e.g., Chaat Masala).

creator: Gurmeet
text: Gurmeet shared an impromptu recipe for Peanut Ridgegourd Chutney. The idea came from having ridgegourd on the counter and deciding to add it to a peanut chutney being made for idlis. The specific ingredients and method for the peanut chutney base are not detailed, but the key is the addition of ridgegourd to a standard peanut chutney.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku shared that black rice is cooked just like regular brown rice: soak overnight, then three whistles in a pressure cooker.

recipe_name: Sugar-Free, Flourless Oatmeal, Apple, and Carrot Bake
creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Ingredients: 2 cups (200g) rolled oats (chopped in a blender), 1 tsp baking powder, 1 cup (240ml) plant-based milk, 1 grated carrot, 9 dried apricots (rinsed with hot water and chopped), 4 Tbsp raisins (rinsed with hot water), 1 grated apple. Optional additions: 1 tsp cinnamon, 0.5 tsp vanilla extract, pinch of salt, 1-2 Tbsp chia seeds or flaxseed meal. Instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). 2. Prepare Oats: Blend rolled oats briefly to a coarse flour/fine flakes consistency. Combine with baking powder (and optional salt/spices). 3. Mix Wet Ingredients: In another bowl, mix grated carrot, grated apple, milk, chopped apricots, and raisins. Let sit for 5-10 minutes. 4. Combine Everything: Mix wet and dry ingredients. Add more milk if too dry. 5. Pour into Baking Dish: Use a small baking dish or loaf pan (lined with parchment). Flatten top. 6. Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until set and lightly golden (toothpick comes out mostly clean). 7. Cool for at least 15-20 minutes before slicing. Storage: Store in fridge up to 5 days, freezes well. Serve as breakfast bar, snack, or healthy dessert.

creator: Group Member
text: A group member suggested exploring local berries in India, which might be healthier than popular Western ones. Amla is highlighted as the healthiest berry. The member also shared an experience with 'black tomato' berries (identified as black nightshade) growing as a weed in their garden, which they found delicious and healthy, despite not liking regular tomatoes. These berries are fragile and cannot be stored or transported.

creator: Multiple Group Members
text: Several ideas were shared for using jackfruit seeds: roasted seeds as a snack, boiled with garlic + red chili chutney, making sabzi like potatoes (chop into 2, sauté onions, haldi, mirchi, then add seeds), sprouted seeds, making 'Bikkand (seeds) sukke', 'bikkand saung', adding to chana for 'ghashi', or making a dry potato-like subzi. A link to a Jackfruit Seed Hummus recipe (https://jollytomato.com/jackfruit-seed-hummus-recipe/) was also shared, with a suggestion to try it without EVOO. Tips for dry roasting include using a pan on the stove (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zINtWlD4cDI) or an air fryer (https://www.youtube.com/shorts/iq0OeLKUqyY), skipping salt or oil. When air frying, it was noted that seeds tend to fly around, so placing them between racks or under a cover is recommended.

creator: Group Member
text: For those who don't do well with cilantro, a member suggested buying various sprouts from farmers markets to use as a garnish instead. These add visual appeal and different flavors, serving as a good alternative.

creator: Uma Venkataraman WFPB
text: Uma Venkataraman WFPB suggested leaving some of the peel in bananas when preparing them, as it is one of the best parts and is loaded with fiber.

creator: Group Member
text: A member shared a recipe for Avocado Kulfi, noting that blending avocado quickly with other ingredients and freezing prevents oxidation, resulting in a nice green kulfi. They suggested switching or adding different fruits/berries like mango, strawberry, or cherry for variety. Initial recipe used Oatly, but it was noted that Oatly often contains added oils and is not WFPB compliant. Suggestions for WFPB alternatives included Eden Soy (soybeans and water only) or using water-soaked organic rolled oats for body. The member planned to try these alternatives.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text: Ingredients: Dry ingredients: Jowar flour, chana flour, ragi flour in a 4:3:3 ratio (total ~100g for 25 biscuits), 1 tsp baking soda, 10g each cocoa powder and carob powder (adjust for desired darkness). Wet ingredients: Cashew milk (homemade), 8-10 dates (blended with milk, adjust for sweetness). Method: 1. Blend dates with cashew milk to make a sweet milk. 2. Use this milk to make a soft, non-sticky dough with the dry ingredients. 3. Roll out the dough and cut into desired shapes. 4. Make impressions with a chopstick (like Hide and Seek biscuits). 5. Press some dark chocolate chips onto the biscuits. 6. Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes. Kids loved them as a good alternative to chocolate and biscuits.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku shared that whisking the ground moong dal batter for a few minutes with a fork was helpful in making Idli somewhat fluffy, without the need for Eno.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku shared six ideas to reduce or eliminate salt in meals, emphasizing that salt is 'The Lazy Man's way of flavoring meals' and that reducing it allows one to taste other subtleties. 1. Naturally high acidic foods: lemon, vinegars. 2. Salt-free mustard. 3. Vegetables with naturally higher sodium: celery, broccoli. 4. Naturally spicy foods: cayenne pepper, chipotle pepper, berbere spice mix, red pepper flakes, jalapenos, chile peppers, ginger. 5. Herbs & dried spices: onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper, minced garlic, fresh onion, thyme, oregano, basil, paprika, cumin, rosemary, mint (fresh or dried). 6. Sea vegetables (nori, dulse) and veggie stock. A follow-up discussion clarified that some non-whole foods like cacao powder, tofu, tempeh, plant-based milks, teas, veggie broth, and vegetable juices are often considered acceptable in WFPB circles, despite not being strictly 'whole'.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text: Gunjan Sahni WFPB shared two frosting recipes for a cake: White frosting: Cashew, tofu, raisins. Pink frosting: Sweet potato, dates, beetroot, peanut butter. She also mentioned making sprinkles from coconut flour mixed with beetroot puree (for pink) and coconut flour mixed with a pinch of turmeric and water (for yellow), which kids enjoyed adding.

creator: Kusum WFPB
text: Kusum WFPB shared a link to a vegan Mishti Doi recipe: https://holycowvegan.net/vegan-mishti-doi/.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Shalini Other Lady WFPB shared modifications for the Plant-Based Mango Cheesecake recipe from Seonkyoung Longest (https://seonkyounglongest.com/plant-based-mango-cheesecake/): The crust does not need maple syrup, and roasted almond flour was used in the base. For the 'cheese' part, coconut cream was reduced to one can and silken tofu was added instead. While maple syrup was used for a non-WFPB group, date syrup would be preferred for WFPB. For the mango layer, 1/2 frozen Kesar mango pulp and 1/2 Kent mangoes were used. Quantities were increased for a larger cake.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 5 Tbsp Ragi, 1.5 cups Water, 1 cup Soy milk, 1.5 Tbsp Almond flour, 3 powdered Cardamom, 3 Tbsp Date syrup, 3 Tbsp Date sugar, Cashews (to garnish). Method: 1. Add ragi and water to a pot, mix well. 2. Place on stove, bring to a gentle boil on slow to medium heat while whisking continuously. 3. Add remaining ingredients (soy milk, almond flour, cardamom, date syrup, date sugar) and continue stirring until the mix thickens and turns shiny (approx. 25-30 minutes). The consistency should be like idli batter. Adjust sweetness to taste. 4. Pour into a 2-3 inch deep container (e.g., bread baking tray). 5. Refrigerate for 2-3 hours. 6. Loosen edges with a knife, invert onto a plate, cut into squares, and garnish with cashew bits. Keep refrigerated. This is a WFPB version of a traditional dessert, originally made with coconut milk.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Gurmeet shared tips for popping amaranth: Use a medium hot pot. Try popping no more than one tablespoon of amaranth at a time. Play with the temperature to find the right heat for popping. If the pot is too hot, the amaranth may burn instead of popping. A specific brand, Anna and Sarah Amaranth (https://a.co/d/ik3vKMT), was recommended as one that pops well. Another member mentioned doing the same with quinoa.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku initiated a discussion on WFPB-compliant coconut substitutes, as coconuts are discouraged by some WFPB luminaries. Members shared ideas: Sharmila Vedam suggested grinding silken tofu with 1-2 Tbsp of coconut (for flavor) for South Indian gravies. Padma suggested grinding a tiny amount of coconut for flavor with roasted daliya for similar taste and texture. Uma Venkataraman WFPB noted fig leaves have a hint of young coconut flavor and can be used to wrap food or in desserts. Ambika suggested celery (plus hemp or cashews) as a substitute in koottu, chutneys, and pachadis, and soaked raw peanuts for 'morekuzhambu'. Ambika also advised adding soaked chia seeds while blending to mask the flavor of coconut substitutes and gradually reducing coconut until the right taste is achieved. Links to Facebook group discussions on coconut substitutes were also provided.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 2 cups popped amaranth (plus extra for rolling), 10-12 dates (soaked in ~4 Tbsp warm water), 4 Tbsp roasted peanuts, 2 Tbsp dried sweet cherries, 0.5 cup soy milk, 2 tsp almond flour. Method: 1. In a blender, combine soaked dates (with soaking water), cherries, peanuts, and half of the soy milk. Blend to a thick paste, adding more milk in batches as needed. 2. Transfer the paste to a mixing bowl. Add popped amaranth and almond flour, mix well to form a cohesive, chapati-consistency dough. 3. Wet palms with a little water, roll the mixture into ladoos. 4. Roll the ladoos in extra popped amaranth. Ladoos are ready to enjoy.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: Lemon, 21 Salute seasoning, dried oregano, dried basil, sumac. Optional additions: apple cider vinegar, peach cider vinegar. This dressing is used for zucchini and described as 'yum and so satisfying'.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Gurmeet discussed vegetable options for a Vegetable Korma, stating that any available vegetables like mushrooms, zucchini, bell peppers, or broccoli can be used. The typical 'must-haves' are potatoes, carrots, peas, and cauliflower. This was in response to a question about replacing Brussels sprouts with cabbage in an Indian dish.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: For vegan tea with oat milk, consider these WFPB notes: (1) Instead of the “Oatly” brand for oat milk, choose “Three Trees” brand (often found in Grocery Outlet for cheap) as Oatly has oil as an ingredient, while Three Trees has a much better ingredient list. (2) Instead of agave syrup, honey, or jaggery (all classified as “Added Sugars”), use homemade date syrup or date paste as a sweetener (dates, date syrup, date sugar & date paste are recommended by Dr. Greger; raisins, dried figs, etc., can also be used for sweetening preparations other than chai).

recipe_name: Understanding Dr. Michael Greger and WFPB Principles
creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Dr. Michael Greger is a prominent figure in Whole Food Plant-Based (WFPB) nutrition. His website, NutritionFacts.org, hosts over 2,000 short videos on nutrition, providing scientific reasoning for WFPB guidelines. He is the author of the bestseller “How Not To Die” and “How Not To Die Cookbook,” which is SOS-Free (without Salt, Oil, and Sugar), using ingredients like miso for salty flavor. Dr. Greger is a Fellow and founding member of the American College of Lifestyle Medicine (ACLM), a medical specialization focusing on lifestyle, particularly 100% vegan WFPB nutrition, free from oil, sugar, ultra-processed foods, and refined grains. He shares his personal story in a 3-minute video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G9Z-gKAvzOY). For discussions on personal health markers, medical conditions, macro-nutrients, and micro-nutrients, members are encouraged to join the “WFPB Chit Chat” group.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text:
For the cheese layer: Blend 1 cup soaked cashews, 1 block silken tofu, 1/2 block firm tofu, 1/2 cup soy yogurt, 1/2 cup date syrup, 1/4 cup maple syrup, 1 tsp pure vanilla extract, 1 tsp agar agar (soaked in room temp water for 10 minutes, then boiled in a pan until it begins to form a gel – psyllium husk could also work), and the rind and juice of one large lemon until smooth. Pour over the base layer and freeze for 3-4 hours or overnight.
For the base layer: Blend 1/2 cup walnuts, 1/2 cup pecans (or replace with walnuts), 1/4 cup almonds, 10 mejdool dates, and 1/2 cup roasted almond flour in a food processor until it resembles breadcrumbs. Do not add water. Press evenly into a thin layer on a springform pan and freeze for a couple of hours.
For the mango layer: Blend 1 cup each of 1/2 frozen Kesar mango pulp from India and 1/2 fresh mangoes until smooth. Pour on top of the 'cheese' layer and freeze for another couple of hours. Decorate with cut mango cubes and slivered almonds. Bring the cheesecake to the fridge an hour before serving.

text: Kanji is a good probiotic drink that can be made year-round. It is considered more palatable than kombucha, which often contains sugar.

creator: Group Member
text: Ingredients: Raw mixed diced or shredded veggies (carrot, beet, cabbage, turnip, etc.) OR boiled diced potatoes. Water, salt, turmeric, hing, black mustard powder, red chili powder, ACV (apple cider vinegar). Optional: grated ginger. Method: Boil water, and when it’s warm, add salt, turmeric, hing, black mustard powder, red chili powder & ACV. Leave it on the countertop. You can add the veggies the same day or the next day. Optional to add grated ginger. Cover the jar with a cloth & keep in the sun for a few hours (if possible). It will start to turn sour on day 3-4. Keep checking & start using. Once it is sour enough, keep it outside for a day or two & then move leftovers to the fridge.

text: Ingredients: TJ's chunky peanut butter, tahini, lemon juice, chili sauce, tamarind paste, a touch of soy sauce, and date syrup to taste. Improvise with what you have.

text: Soak buckwheat overnight. The next day, rinse it well 3-4 times in water. Then add fresh fruit, rehydrated berries, and miscellaneous powders like cardamom powder, cinnamon powder, fennel powder, ginger powder (whatever your taste buds like). You may add some dates or dried figs or date syrup or date sugar for extra sweetness. The buckwheat is eaten raw after overnight soaking and rinsing.

text: For Oats and Tofu Patty: Use a 50-50 ratio of silken tofu to oats flour. Blend silken tofu to a paste and add to the whole mixture with a little water for desired consistency. Veggies also form a significant part.

text: No overnight soaking required for this Millet Poha. Cook millet less if you want it more chewy. The tempering includes cumin seeds, green chillies, and curry leaves. Add potatoes, cilantro, and peanuts.

creator: Group Member
text: Ingredients: 1 cup Rajgira (Amaranth) flour, 1 large steamed Sweet potato (Japanese or regular), 1 carrot grated (hand grate for easy blending), a handful of arugula leaves chopped fine, a handful of cilantro leaves chopped fine, chilies chopped fine according to taste, peanut or pecan powder, salt to taste. Method: Mash the sweet potato well, add all the ingredients and mix well into a ball. If it’s too mushy, add some more amaranth flour. Split into 4-6 portions. Heat the tava (cast iron, seasoned with oil and wiped away). With wet hands, either pat each portion one by one directly on the tava, or pat it into a thalipeeth on a silicon mat and gently lift to place on the tava. Cover and let it cook for 2-3 minutes. Flip it and let the other side cook. Enjoy warm with chutney.

creator: Group Member
text: Ingredients: 1 large Granny Smith apple, a large handful cilantro, chillies to taste, 1 clove garlic, a handful of roasted peanuts or pecans, salt. Method: Grind all ingredients in a blender until smooth.

creator: Leena Menon WFPB
text: Ingredients: 1 Chinese eggplant, 2 roasted garlic cloves, 1/4 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp parsley, 1 tsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp tahini, 1/4 cup yogurt, 1/8 tsp salt. Method: Roast eggplant and peel off skin. Mash and add all ingredients.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 1/2 cup tri-colored quinoa, 4 tbsp chana daal, 3 tbsp toor daal, 3 tbsp moong daal, 1/2 cup spinach, 2 green chillies, 1/2 inch ginger, 1 tsp garam masala powder (to taste), 1 tsp coriander+cumin powder (to taste), 1/3 tsp turmeric powder, Himalayan salt to taste, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 chopped carrot, 1/4 cup green peas, 1/4 cup chopped green beans, 2 chopped garlic cloves. Method: 1. Rinse and soak quinoa and daals for 30 minutes. 2. Blanch the spinach, add green chillies and ginger, then grind to a paste. 3. Pressure cook the soaked quinoa+daals+turmeric powder and salt until soft (5 minutes after the first whistle). 4. In a pot, dry temper the cumin, add garlic, and sauté for a minute. 5. Add peas and carrots, cook for 5 minutes. 6. Add the pureed spinach, stir, cook for 1-2 minutes, then add garam masala, coriander, and cumin powder. Now add the cooked quinoa+daals and stir. 7. Turn off the heat and enjoy!

recipe_name: Pistachio Cake Sweetness Tip & Tres Leches Modification

text: For optimum sweetness in pistachio cake, increase the sweetener quantity to 1.5 times the original recipe. If the cake is not sweet enough, it can be transformed into a Tres Leches cake by adding date syrup to your choice of plant-based milk and pouring it over the cake.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 4 medium bananas, 30 toothpicks. Chocolate sauce: 12 soaked dates, 2 tbsp cacao powder, 2/3 cup water, 6 tbsp date syrup, 2 tbsp almond butter. Toppings: Popped Amaranth (or other suggestions below). Method: 1. Peel bananas, cut into thick slices, insert toothpicks, and freeze for 2-3 hours. 2. For the chocolate sauce, soak dates in 2/3 cup hot water for 30 minutes. 3. Blend soaked dates and water to a smooth paste, adding more water if needed. 4. In a pot, add date syrup to 1/4 cup water and cook on low heat until slightly thickened. 5. Add the blended chocolate date mix and almond butter to the pot. Stir and cook for 1-2 minutes. 6. Turn off heat, let the chocolate sauce cool, then pour into a glass bowl. 7. Dip each frozen banana slice into the sauce, then gently roll into popped amaranth or sprinkle with chopped nuts. 8. Drizzle extra sauce on the pops, freeze for 20 minutes, and serve. Additional topping suggestions: 2 tbsp roasted and crushed pistachios, 2 tbsp roasted and crushed peanuts, 1 tbsp roasted sesame seeds.

creator: Group Member
text: Ingredients: 500g sprouted whole grain flour (approximately 3 cups and 2 Tbs; whole wheat works well too, or any whole grain flour), 2 tsp Himalayan pink salt, 2 Tbs unfed sourdough starter from the fridge, 1 ¾ cups room temperature water (adjust based on needs), ¼ cup each of sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, black or white sesame seeds, hemp seeds, and ground flaxseed.
