creator: Group Member
text: Sourdough bread can be made salt-free, but the taste will be less salted. Note that fermentation time also changes with no salt, so experimentation is needed.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 1 tsp active dry yeast, 1 tsp maple syrup, 2 1/4 cups + 2 tbsp whole wheat flour (e.g., One Degree Organic Sprouted Whole Wheat Flour). Method: 1. Measure 1 1/4 cups warm (105F) water, stir in yeast and maple syrup. Cover and place in a dark place for 1-2 hours until foamy and cloudy. 2. In a medium bowl, stir together 2 1/4 cups flour. Stir the yeast mixture into the flour until a batter-like dough forms. Stir vigorously for 30 seconds until smooth. Cover and chill dough overnight. 3. Two hours before baking, line an 8-inch square baking pan with parchment paper, dusting with 2 tbsp flour. Pour chilled dough into the pan. Cover with a clean kitchen towel and let rise in a warm place for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, or until doubled in volume. 4. Preheat oven to 425 F. Using damp fingers, press dimples all over the top of the focaccia. Add seasonings like Italian seasoning and Herbes de Provence. 5. Bake for 35-40 minutes or until browned and firm on top. Use parchment paper to remove from pan; cool on a wire rack. Peel away parchment paper once cool enough to handle. Cool completely before serving. The texture of the bread was soft to the touch.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 3/4 packet spaghetti (cooked per instructions), 4 chopped garlic cloves, 1/2 chopped red onion, 1/4 chopped yellow squash, 5 chopped baby portabella mushrooms, 2 chopped tomatoes, 2 medium chopped carrots, 1 tbsp 21 Salute seasoning, 1 tbsp Italian seasoning, 2 tsp dried parsley, 3-4 tbsp salt-free tomato paste. Method: 1. Dry sauté garlic and onions in a pan, adding water if needed, until translucent. 2. Add the rest of the veggies, cook with a lid on until slightly softened. 3. Add chopped tomatoes and tomato paste, stir, and cook with a lid on until tomatoes soften. 4. Remove lid, add all herbs, and cook until the sauce comes together and water dries up a little. 5. Stir in the cooked pasta, adding some pasta water if it looks too dry. 6. Enjoy! Notes: Bell pepper, zucchini, and edamame can also be added. Use herbs of your choice.

creator: Group Member
text: Ingredients: 1 box silken tofu, 2 boiled sweet potatoes, 1 tbsp cacao powder (optional: add 1 tsp instant coffee), vanilla splash, 1 tbsp agave or maple syrup or mejdool dates, splash of vegan milk. Method: Blend all ingredients until smooth. Chill in the fridge for an hour. Toppings: cocoa nibs, raspberry, nuts, coconut strips, etc.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Ingredients: 1 cup ragi flour, 5-6 large ripe bananas, 1 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp baking soda, 1/4 tsp salt, ¼ cup walnuts/pecans/almonds chopped or crushed, 1/4 cup plant yogurt, 1/4 cup lukewarm water (can be replaced with vegan milk). Extra walnuts/pecans/almonds or sugar-free chocolate for garnish. Method: Bake at 350 F for 25-30 minutes. If using a smaller oven, cover the top with a piece of parchment or foil after 20 minutes to prevent burning.

creator: Group Member
text: Ingredients: 2 cups oats (blended into flour), 1 or 2 smashed bananas, 1/4 tsp baking soda. Method: Blend oats to flour. Smash bananas. Mix all ingredients. Put it in the oven & bake it.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Microwaving is considered acceptable in Whole Food Plant-Based circles. Dr. Greger has videos that provide assurance on this topic (https://nutritionfacts.org/?s=microwave). For example, all of my cooked meals during the last 2-3 years were prepared in a microwave.

creator: Prathima WFPB
text:
This dessert is made with eyeball measurements. 

Base: Combine almond flour, cashews, walnuts, vanilla powder, and dates. Coarsely powder these ingredients (blend nuts coarsely before adding dates). Tap the mixture into a mold to create the base layer. This can be baked for a few minutes or used raw.

Mango Layer: Use frozen and fresh mango, and cashews. Create one layer of only mango puree, then top with chopped mango. Dates were not needed as the mango was ripe, but can be added if extra sweetness is desired.

Blueberry Layer: Use frozen blueberries, any nuts, and dates. Top with frozen blueberries.

The consistency of the layers is thick, so a divider is not needed for clean edges.

creator: WFPB member
text:
Ingredients: Cucumber, colored peppers, red onion, carrot, red cabbage, home-grown ash gourd, cauliflower, cilantro, coarsely crushed peanuts, salt, lime juice, white pepper powder, and chopped grapes.

Method: Chop all vegetables finely. Mix with coarsely crushed peanuts, salt, lime juice, and white pepper powder. Top with chopped grapes.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
Method: Soak whole amaranth overnight. Boil it either in a pot for 25-30 minutes (stir constantly until thick) or in a pressure cooker for 10 minutes after the first whistle. Gurmeet preferred the taste of the pot-cooked version. 

Sweetener: Add blended dates and water, cardamom powder, allspice powder, and cinnamon. 

Serving: Top with fruits. Plant-based milk is optional.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
Ingredients: Firm tofu (water drained and crumbled), spring onions, chopped red onion, garlic, chopped zucchini, baby spinach, goda masala, coriander+cumin powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, green chili, mint leaves, cilantro, chopped tomato, snap peas, red radish. Any other vegetables like mushrooms, bell peppers, or broccoli can be added.

Method: Dry sauté the chopped onions and the spring onion bulb. Add the rest of the vegetables and spinach. Cook with a lid on for 3-4 minutes. Now add the crumbled tofu, tomatoes, mint leaves, and all the dry spice powders. Stir and cook until the water dries up a little bit. Garnish with cilantro.

recipe_name: Serving Tofu Bhurjee in Napa Cabbage Boats
creator: WFPB member
text: A cooking tip for Tofu Bhurjee is to serve it in napa cabbage leaves, which act as a 'boat.' The cool, crisp cabbage leaf adds a nice contrast and makes it fun to eat. Zucchini boats are also suggested as an alternative.

recipe_name: Homemade Soy Milk and Yogurt Discussion
creator: Group Member
text: A group member inquired about suitable soy milk brands in the US for making homemade soy yogurt and whether store-bought cashew yogurt could be used as a starter. Gunjan Sahni WFPB suggested that making soy milk at home is 'super easy.'

creator: Shilpa Mulberry WFPB
text:
Ingredients: A lot of curry leaves, cumin seeds, 1 tbsp peanuts, pumpkin seeds, white sesame seeds, brown sesame seeds, black sesame seeds, sunflower seeds, Dalia (roasted split chickpeas), and a pinch of black salt (to taste).

Method: Dry roast a generous amount of curry leaves. Grind them. Dry roast cumin seeds and grind them into a fine powder. Dry roast 1 tablespoon each of peanuts, pumpkin seeds, white sesame seeds, brown sesame seeds, black sesame seeds, sunflower seeds, and Dalia, then grind them coarsely. Mix all the ground ingredients together. Add a pinch of black salt to taste.

recipe_name: Enhancing Pistachio Cake to Tres Leches Style
creator: Gurmeet, Shruti Mirashi Joshi
text:
To make a pistachio cake sweeter or transform it into a Tres Leches style cake, pour sweetened plant-based milk over it, either while serving or by soaking the cake. If you prefer the pistachio cake alone, increase the sweetener quantity by 1.5 times for optimum sweetness.

Options for sweetened soy milk:
1. Add a thick paste of soaked cashews and raisins.
2. Add maple syrup and cashew butter.
3. Add date syrup and cashew butter.

Adding cashews to the milk is recommended for an enhanced dessert eating experience.

creator: Prathima WFPB, Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Prathima WFPB suggested creating a section on the group's website or a Google Doc for WFPB store-bought options, particularly for school snacks for kids. Gurmeet Singh Manku agreed, proposing that members contribute their findings to a Google Doc which could later be converted into articles.

creator: Kusum WFPB
text: Method: Soak a tablespoon of amaranth seeds in water for 24 hours, changing the water every 12 hours. After soaking, drain the water using a strainer and let the seeds sit in the strainer overnight, covered with a lid. Rinse again in the strainer and leave for another 10-12 hours. Finally, spread the seeds on a paper towel and cover lightly to allow air circulation. A sprouting jar can also be used. This method is an experiment to potentially grow them to microgreens.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB, Shruti Mirashi Joshi
text:
To give pav bhaji a buttery or cheesy taste using WFPB ingredients, prepare a spread:

Ingredients: Half a boiled potato, 10 soaked cashews, 1 tbsp nutritional yeast, 2-3 black peppercorns, a little lemon juice or vinegar, and optional salt.

Method: Pulse all ingredients nicely until a soft, butter-like consistency is achieved. Add 1-2 tablespoons of this spread on top of steaming hot pav bhaji just before serving. This spread is noted to taste more like cheese than butter and can also be used for vegan grilled cheese sandwiches. Alternatively, a little almond butter can be added to the final pav bhaji preparation.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text:
Ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas (do NOT use canned or cooked), 1 cup fresh parsley leaves (stems removed), 3/4 cup fresh cilantro, 1/2 cup fresh dill (stems removed), 1 medium white onion (quartered), 2-3 garlic cloves (peeled), 1 tsp ground black pepper, 1 tbsp ground cumin, 1 tbsp ground coriander, 1 tsp cayenne pepper, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, 2-3 tbsp rice flour, salt to taste.

Method: Soak the chickpeas for 7-8 hours or overnight. In a food processor, run all ingredients except sesame seeds, rice flour, and salt until the mixture resembles medium breadcrumbs. Transfer to a bowl and add the sesame seeds, rice flour, and salt. Mix well. Form into flat 1.5-inch round discs. Air fry at the nugget setting at 350°F for 10 minutes per side. Serve with fresh babaghanouj, hummus, and salad.

creator: Satvic Swetha Kogatam
text:
Ingredients: 1.5 cups Jowar, a handful of peanuts, 3-4 cups water, mustard seeds, jeera (cumin seeds), urad dal, green chili, onion (optional), red chili, curry leaves, vegetables (carrot, peas, corn, etc.), salt, sesame seeds, roasted peanuts, chopped coriander, lemon juice. Grated fresh coconut is optional for a satvic version, skip for WFPB.

Method:
1. Wash 1.5 cups of Jowar and soak overnight.
2. Discard the soaked water. Add a handful of peanuts and pressure cook the Jowar with 3-4 cups of water for 8-9 whistles (or use Instant Pot bean/chili mode). Check if Jowar can be mashed with two fingers; if not, cook for a couple more whistles.
3. In a pan, dry sauté mustard seeds, jeera, urad dal, green chili, onion (if using), red chili, and curry leaves.
4. Add chopped vegetables like carrot, peas, corn, etc., and salt. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
5. Add the boiled Jowar (discarding any remaining water) and cook for another 3-4 minutes on medium flame with the lid on.
6. Sprinkle with sesame seeds, some roasted peanuts, chopped coriander, and lemon juice. Serve.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku's mom
text:
Ingredients: 3 cups small pieces of apple, beetroot, and whole plums (deseeded); 1 cup deseeded soaked dates; 2 cloves; 1/4 tsp ginger powder; 1/4 tsp cinnamon powder; 1 bay leaf; 1/2 tsp cardamom powder.

Method:
1. Boil or steam the apple, beetroot, and deseeded plums.
2. Grind or blend the cooked fruit and vegetable mixture with the deseeded soaked dates.
3. Cook the mixture in a pot with cloves, ginger powder, cinnamon powder, and bay leaf, stirring continuously until it reaches a thick consistency.
4. Turn off the flame and add cardamom powder. Mix well.
5. Cool the jam and serve with Whole Food Plant-Based bread, roti, paratha, puri, or cookies.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text:
Ingredients: 100 gms tofu, 40-50 gms besan (chickpea flour), black salt, a pinch of baking powder, 100-120 ml water.

Method: Blend all ingredients properly until smooth. Pour the mixture onto a very hot pan. Let it cook on medium to high flame for 1-2 minutes on both sides. Cover and cook until done.

creator: Shruti Mirashi Joshi
text: Shruti Mirashi Joshi successfully made a WFPB Tiramisu using a ChatGPT recipe, noting that it turned out 'pretty decent.' She plans to fine-tune the recipe and share it with the group sometime next month.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
Ingredients: Pulp of cooked drumsticks, toor daal, moringa leaves, tomato, tamarind, garlic, turmeric powder, mustard seeds, curry leaves, red chili.

Method: Cook drumsticks, toor daal, moringa leaves, tomato, tamarind, garlic, and turmeric powder. Blend these ingredients to a soup consistency. Prepare a dry tempering with mustard seeds, curry leaves, and red chili. Add the tempering to the soup.

creator: Prathima WFPB
text: This recipe is an adaptation of the Pistachio Cake from addictedtodates.com/pistachio-cake/. Prathima WFPB used whole wheat flour and soy milk, and skipped oil and sugar in her version.

recipe_name: Homemade Peanut Milk and Pulp Usage
creator: Satvic Swetha Kogatam, Kusum WFPB
text: To make peanut milk, use a ratio of 1:4 (soaked peanuts to water), or 1:3. The peanut skin does not need to be peeled. A nut milk maker can be used for grinding and straining. The leftover peanut pulp is versatile and can be used to make crackers, laddoos (by adding dates), dried for later use, or incorporated into chapati dough.

recipe_name: Resource for Growing Microgreens at Home
creator: WFPB member
text: A resource for growing microgreens at home was shared: https://plantbasedlosangeles.org/growing-micro-greens-at-home/. Broccoli and mustard microgreens were specifically mentioned as being grown at home.

creator: WFPB member
text:
Ingredients: Oats, soy milk, blueberry, pomegranate, apple, banana, walnuts, almonds, flaxseed, chia seeds, pumpkin seeds, and sunflower seeds.

Method: Combine all ingredients and soak overnight. Serve for breakfast.

recipe_name: Pineapple Oats Cake with Cream Topping
creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text:
Cake Ingredients: 200 gms rolled oats, 100 gms pineapple chunks (instead of juice), 50 gms peanut butter, a pinch of salt, 1 tsp baking powder, 100-150 ml water (approx), 100 gms dates.

Cream Topping Ingredients: 1 boiled potato, a handful of cashews, 2 dates, some water, vanilla extract.

Method:
1. For the cake: Pulse all cake ingredients together until combined. 
2. Place thin pineapple slices at the bottom of a baking pan. Pour half of the batter over them. Add a second layer of pineapple slices, then cover with the remaining batter.
3. Bake at 180°C for 50 minutes. After 50 minutes, flip the cake over and bake for another 10 minutes.
4. For the cream topping: Blend the boiled potato, cashews, dates, some water, and vanilla extract until nicely smooth. This cream helps balance the sweetness of the cake if it's too sweet for your palate.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
Ingredients: Arbi (colocasia), green chili, chopped onions, cumin seeds, red chili powder, cumin+coriander powder, dry mango powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, cilantro.

Method: Pressure cook the arbi. Prepare an oil-free tempering by dry sautéing green chili, chopped onions, and cumin seeds. Add red chili powder, cumin+coriander powder, dry mango powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Add some water to the dry masalas to create a thick slurry before adding it to the sabzi. Garnish with cilantro. This is a quick preparation.

recipe_name: Cooking Tips for Cluster Beans (Guar Phali)
creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB, Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text:
Cluster beans (also known as Guar Phali, Guara Di phalli, chikkudukaya, chavlikai, gorikayi, kothavarakkai, or guvarsing) are rich in soluble fiber. Guar gum, a thickener used in many processed foods, comes from this bean.

Cooking Tips:
*   Gunjan Sahni WFPB cooks them with lots of garlic and green chili.
*   Shalini Other Lady WFPB strings the beans, steams them, and then sautés them with roasted besan (chickpea flour) and amchur powder (dry mango powder).

creator: Uma Venkataraman WFPB, WFPB member
text:
Ingredients: Silken tofu, curry leaves, green chilies, lemon juice, boiled vegetables (e.g., pushnikka/winter melon), optional celery stick, optional hemp, optional methi seeds, optional red chili, optional date, optional soy milk.

Method (Uma Venkataraman WFPB's version): Blend silken tofu, curry leaves, green chilies, and lemon juice. Add boiled vegetables (winter melon is a favorite and tastes better if soaked in the blended contents for a day). The mixture is not cooked, though leftovers can be warmed. Coconut is omitted for a WFPB version.

Variations (WFPB member's suggestions):
*   Add a celery stick and hemp as a replacement for coconut.
*   For a Kerala-style version, roast methi seeds and red chili, then blend with celery, hemp, soy milk, lemon juice, and a date. Serve with raw mango and winter melon.

recipe_name: Homemade Soy Milk and Yogurt Making Tips
creator: WFPB member
text:
Tips for making homemade soy milk and yogurt:
*   A NAMA juicer can make the process easier and less messy compared to using a blender and muslin cloth.
*   Soy milk needs boiling right after making it. It's best to use a portion of the freshly boiled milk to set yogurt immediately.
*   Soak organic soybeans (e.g., from Amazon) overnight, then give them a quick boil before milking them to reduce their strong flavor.
*   Alternatively, a Soyabella machine can be used, which boils, grinds, and strains all in one small machine.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB's daughter
text:
Ingredients: Soy curd, pink guava, apple, other fruits for topping.

Method: Blend soy curd with pink guava and apple. Chill for some time to allow it to thicken. Serve with a few fruits as toppings.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text: Gunjan Sahni WFPB recommends a high-speed 22,000 RPM juicer mixer grinder with a full copper motor and stainless steel blades (link: https://amzn.in/d/eJj881Q). While not extremely powerful, it is good for shakes, smoothies, and yogurt, and is easy enough for an 11-year-old to use without problems.

recipe_name: Date Sugar and Date Dhibs Recommendations
creator: Group Members
text: For organic date sugar, the 'Date Lady' brand is recommended, available on Amazon and in most grocery stores. Date Dhibs (date syrup), such as the Bateel brand, are also mentioned as a favored sweetener.

recipe_name: Shakarkandi Chhole Chaat with Fresh Herbs
creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: This preparation is a variation of 'Shakarkandi Chhole Chaat.' Instead of traditional chutneys, it uses generous quantities of fresh herbs (dill, cilantro, curry leaves, gongura leaves, basil), lemon, and dry spice mixes.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: For veggie medleys or salads, hard vegetables such as potatoes, sweet potatoes, yams, carrots, beetroot, parsnips, hard squashes, and sweet onion should be steamed. Leafy greens are almost always kept raw, but can sometimes be steamed (e.g., mustard greens). All other ingredients are used raw.

creator: WFPB member
text:
Ingredients: Spinach, arugula, green apple, lemon, fresh turmeric, cucumbers, Amla (Indian gooseberry), and beetroot.

Method: (Implied) Blend or juice all ingredients together.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: To cook whole amaranth, soak it overnight and then boil it in the morning. This is an alternative method to popping amaranth.

creator: WFPB member
text: A group member inquired about how to pop amaranth successfully, specifically to replicate 'Sohum’s Rajgira ladoo.' Another member mentioned their mother pops it in a normal pan and plans to try and share the process if successful. The method for popping amaranth is not yet provided in detail.

creator: Group Members
text: A discussion arose regarding how laddoos can achieve a crispy texture, especially when wet ingredients are not cooked. It was noted that such laddoos might not typically be crunchy, but using maple syrup could potentially help achieve a crispier texture.

creator: WFPB member
text:
Ingredients: Quinoa, chopped onion, tomatoes, bell peppers, chilies, garlic, curry leaves, peanuts, sambar powder.

Method: Sauté the chopped onion, tomatoes, bell peppers, chilies, garlic, curry leaves, peanuts, and sambar powder. Add boiled quinoa and sauté for a few more minutes.

recipe_name: Navratri Fasting and Guided Fasting Resources
creator: Satvic Swetha Kogatam, Kusum WFPB, WFPB member, WFPB member
text: Discussion about Navratri fasting, with members expressing interest in raw plant-based diets, steamed meals (with exceptions), or 1-2 meals a day, as well as water fasting. Information was shared about guided fasting programs run by 'Lalit ji (LMK)' twice a year. These programs recommend eating approximately 500 calories once a day, provide sample meal pictures, and include educational posts on fasting, its effects on the body, and related topics (protein, carbs, etc.). A WhatsApp group link for LMK's health group for Navratri was also shared.

creator: WFPB member
text: Flat beans, also known as Sem or purple hyacinth beans, can be cooked like any other beans. A group member mentioned growing both green and purple varieties in their yard.

creator: Group Member
text: Combine chopped onion, tomatoes, bell peppers, chilies, garlic, curry leaves, peanuts, and sambar powder. Sauté the mixture. Add boiled quinoa and sauté for a few more minutes.

recipe_name: Navratri Fasting / Raw Plant-Based Diet Discussion
creator: Satvic Swetha Kogatam
text: Satvic Swetha Kogatam is planning Navratri upavas (fasting) and wants to try a raw plant-based diet, with occasional steamed meals, 1-2 meals a day. She is looking for ideas and interested individuals to brainstorm a balanced 9-day diet plan.

creator: Srinath
text: Lalit ji (LMK) runs guided fasting courses twice a year. His recommendations include eating ~500 calories once a day, with a sample meal pic posted daily. The same meal might be recommended for 9 days, allowing for replacements. He also posts long messages about fasting, its effects on the body, and related topics (protein/carb, etc.). There's a WhatsApp group for this.

creator: Group Member
text: Use a 1:4 grain to water ratio. Cook in an Instant Pot on Porridge Mode. The auto-selected time is usually 20 minutes. Add a few dates for sweetness. This method also works for steel-cut oats.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Use a 1 cup amaranth to 3 to 3.5 cups water ratio (eyeballed). Cook on the stove top for about 25 minutes, stirring intermittently. Blend 4-5 dates in water and add to the porridge along with cardamom and nutmeg powders.

creator: Group Member
text: Dry roast seeds (used whole) and flour. Add warm plant milk, cardamom powder, and date paste. Let it cook until done.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Prepare a batter using urad dal (lighter color) or mung dal (yellower color). Add some vegetables, lots of seeds, and spices to the batter. Before baking, add a packet of Eno. Bake in a muffin pan coated with minimal oil. After baking, soak the wadas in hot water for 20-25 minutes before serving with soy yogurt.

recipe_name: Sourcing Purple Sweet Potato Buckwheat Noodles
creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Purple sweet potato buckwheat noodles can be found on Amazon by searching for 'purple sweet potato buckwheat noodles'.

recipe_name: Incorporating Mushrooms with Mushroom Mix Tea
creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Mushroom mix tea is a good way to incorporate mushrooms into the diet, especially if one doesn't like the taste or flavor of common mushrooms like white button, cremini, or shiitake. Many mushroom mixes are available in the market to sample and find a preferred one.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Blackcurrant powder (from 'ribes nigrum') can be purchased from Amazon. It is important to note that these are different from 'black currants' which are small black raisins. Dr. Greger's videos on blackcurrants are also a good resource.

recipe_name: Sourcing Kitchen Tools (Fine Mesh Strainer, Kitchen Shears)
creator: Group Member
text: For washing amaranth, a fine mesh strainer is recommended. Kitchen shears are also useful. Both can be found on Amazon by searching for 'fine mesh strainer' and 'kitchen shears'.

recipe_name: Steamed Kabocha Squash with Lemon & Black Pepper
creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Steam kabocha squash slices in a microwave. Place slices in a bowl with a little water, cover with a microwave-safe lid (like the one linked: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B087D65D8Q). Steam for 3 minutes, then check, turn, and steam for another 2-3 minutes. Season with lemon and black pepper. Optional additions: soaked barberries or golden berries, or green chutney and some greens.

recipe_name: Essential Kitchen Tools for WFPB Prep (Nakiri Knife, Cutting Board)
creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: For efficient WFPB food preparation, a Nakiri knife is highly recommended for slicing, chopping, dicing, and mincing fruits and vegetables. It's advisable to invest in a high-quality Nakiri knife (upwards of $100) and a honing rod for maintenance. A simple utility knife is sufficient for other tasks. Also, a large-sized, high-quality wooden cutting board (e.g., teak) is suggested.

recipe_name: Spice Grinder vs. Blender for WFPB Kitchen
creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Spice grinders are small and best for dry grinding spices. While a small amount of chutney might be made, for wet grinding (blending wet ingredients), a small-sized blender like a Nutribullet is more suitable.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text:
Various purple fruits and vegetables can be sourced from different places:
*   **San Ramon Farmers Market:** Purple cauliflower, purple cabbage, eggplant, purple basil, purple sweet potatoes, purple kale.
*   **Costco:** Frozen blueberries and blackberries.
*   **Sprouts and Felipe's:** Purple potatoes.
*   **Sprouts (sometimes):** Purple arugula and purple asparagus.
*   **Amazon:** Blackcurrant powder.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text:
**Ingredients:** 500g raw bananas, thinly sliced. For the spice mix: 2-3 tbsp jowar atta, salt to taste, spices like black pepper, garlic powder, red chili powder (adjust to desired flavor).
**Method:**
1.  Place thinly sliced raw bananas in a box.
2.  In a separate bowl, combine jowar atta, salt, and desired spices.
3.  Sprinkle some water over the banana slices.
4.  Add the spice mix to the bananas.
5.  Close the lid of the box and shake well to ensure all chips are nicely coated.
6.  Store the sealed box in the freezer for 2 hours.
7.  Preheat air fryer to 200°C (390°F).
8.  Air fry the banana chips for 15-18 minutes, shaking the basket 2 times during cooking, until crispy. Thin slices will be crispier.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text:
**Yields:** 8-10 cookies.
**Ingredients:**
*   **Dry:** 1 cup (100g) oat flour, ½ cup (60g) ragi flour, ½ cup (60g) chana flour, 1 cup (70g) soy/pea protein powder, 1 tsp cinnamon, ½ tsp salt, ½ tsp baking powder, ½ tsp baking soda.
*   **Wet:** ½ cup (120g) date paste, 3 tbsp flaxseed meal + 9 tbsp water (for flax eggs), 6 tbsp (90ml) plant milk (adjust as needed), 1 tsp vanilla extract.
*   **Nuts & Seeds:** 2 tbsp chopped almonds, 2 tbsp chopped cashews, 2 tbsp pumpkin seeds, 2 tbsp sunflower seeds, 1 tbsp chia seeds.
**Method:**
1.  Prepare flax eggs by mixing 3 tbsp flaxseed meal with 9 tbsp water and letting it rest for 5 minutes.
2.  In a large bowl, mix all dry ingredients.
3.  In another bowl, stir all wet ingredients together.
4.  Combine the wet and dry ingredients to form a thick dough, adjusting with plant milk or flour if necessary.
5.  Fold in the nuts and seeds.
6.  Shape the dough into 8-10 cookies.
7.  Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 15–18 minutes.
8.  Allow cookies to cool completely before storing.
**Variations:**
*   **Chocolate flavor:** Add carob powder or cocoa to the cookie dough.
*   **Lemon cookies:** Add lemon zest and a few drops of lemon juice to the dough.

creator: Leena Menon WFPB
text:
**Mushroom Preparation:** Sprinkle mushrooms with cayenne pepper, garlic powder, and salt. Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 15 minutes.
**Aioli Sauce Ingredients:** 0.25 cup soaked cashews, 0.25 cup raw cauliflower, 1 tsp mustard (brown mustard used), 2 cloves garlic, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 0.25 tsp chili powder, salt to taste, water to blend.
**Method:** Blend all aioli sauce ingredients until smooth.
**Assembly:** Add arugula to the sandwich along with the baked mushrooms and aioli sauce.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Slice cabbage horizontally into ½-inch thick rounds. Microwave for 3 minutes. Spread Kashmiri chili powder and any other desired spices. Roast in an oven, air fryer, or on a cast iron griddle until soft inside and crispy outside.

recipe_name: Vegan Paneer from Lauki and Safed Chana
creator: Group Member
text: A technique for making WFPB vegan 'paneer' using lauki (bottle gourd) and safed chana (white chickpeas) was discussed, based on an external Hindi video. The method involves skipping oil for tempering and cream in the gravy. Gurmeet Singh Manku's mom successfully made this 'paneer' and used it in Matar 'Paneer' Sabzi.

creator: Shruti Mirashi Joshi
text: A WFPB 'cake' made by carving a watermelon as the base and decorating it with various fresh fruits. Jicama can be used as a white fruit for decoration. Cookie cutters can be used to cut fruit into shapes (e.g., stars). This is a visually appealing and healthy alternative to traditional cakes.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text:
**Ingredients:** Grated raw papaya, jeera (cumin seeds), methi (fenugreek seeds), mustard seeds, coriander powder, turmeric powder, chilies, grated ginger, amchur powder (dry mango powder), date syrup, fresh chopped coriander for garnish.
**Method:**
1.  Grate the raw papaya.
2.  Temper with jeera, methi, and mustard seeds.
3.  Add coriander powder, turmeric powder, chilies, and grated ginger.
4.  Cook until the papaya is soft.
5.  Stir in amchur powder and some date syrup.
6.  Garnish with fresh chopped coriander.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
**Ingredients:** 4-5 tbsp ragi flour, 2.5 cups water, cardamom powder, date paste (made by blending 5 dates with some water), 1 grated cucumber.
**Method:**
1.  Add ragi flour to 2.5 cups of water and stir well to dissolve all lumps.
2.  Cook this mixture with cardamom powder, stirring intermittently for 15-20 minutes.
3.  Add the date paste and cook for another 6 minutes.
4.  Stir in 1 grated cucumber and cook for an additional 4-5 minutes until ready.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text:
**Cake Ingredients:**
*   **Dry:** 100g oat flour, 20-30g ragi flour, pinch of salt, 1 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp baking soda, 20-25g cocoa powder.
*   **Wet:** 100g boiled sweet potato, 100g pitted dates, 50-100ml water (for smooth consistency), ½ tsp vinegar.
**Method:**
1.  Blend dry ingredients separately.
2.  Blend wet ingredients separately until smooth.
3.  Combine wet and dry ingredients using a cut and fold method.
4.  Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 40 minutes.
5.  Let the cake cool completely before frosting.

recipe_name: WFPB Chocolate Sweet Potato Cake Frosting
creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text:
**Frosting Ingredients:** 100g boiled sweet potato, 50g dates, 15-20g cocoa powder, 50g nut butter, pinch of salt, about 100ml non-dairy milk (for proper blending).
**Method:**
1.  Blend all frosting ingredients until smooth.
2.  Cool the frosting.
3.  Once the cake is completely cool, apply the frosting.
4.  Let the frosted cake sit in the fridge for 2-3 hours for optimal taste.
5.  Decorate with dark chocolate and nuts if desired.

creator: Satvic Swetha Kogatam
text: A group member is looking for recommendations for a sandwich maker that is not non-stick, questioning if such an appliance exists.

creator: Group Member
text: Break tempeh into pieces, season with Indian seasonings, and air fry until crisp. This air-fried tempeh can be used as a topping for curries or soups, or as a substitute for dal in South Indian 'paruppu usuli'. The cooking time in the air fryer can be adjusted based on the desired crispness for the specific dish.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Radish leaves are versatile. Wash, dry, and chop them finely. Steam in an Instant Pot for 10 minutes, then cool and freeze for later use. They can be incorporated into jowar or millet rotis, besan pakodas, added to dal, or sautéed with spices.

recipe_name: Refeeding Protocol After Water Fasting (True North Guidelines)
creator: Leena Menon WFPB
text: Following water fasting, True North guidelines for refeeding suggest starting with juices. Recommended juice ingredients include watermelon, apple, celery, and cucumber, or combinations thereof. Celery is particularly important as it naturally contains sodium and acts as an electrolyte. For day 2 of refeeding, only raw, SOS-free (salt, oil, sugar-free) meals are recommended, avoiding grains and starchy vegetables. During the fast itself, only water was consumed, without additional electrolytes or supplements.

creator: Group Member
text: A WFPB pizza can be made at home using a base made from moong dal. Masoor dal is suggested to work even better for the base.

recipe_name: Simple Fresh Salad with Lime & Mint Dressing
creator: Gurmeet
text:
**Ingredients:** Fresh chopped garlic, mint leaves, onion, fresh sweet corn, salad mix, lettuce, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, golden berries, grapes, and apples.
**Dressing:** Fresh lime juice.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text:
A versatile, no-tomato soup inspired by Northern Italian cuisine. Ingredients can be adapted based on availability. 

**Ingredients:**
*   1 large red onion
*   2 cups watermelon rinds (peeled with a peeler)
*   1 cup collard stems
*   2 cloves of garlic
*   Bell peppers
*   2 cups soaked and boiled white lima beans (2 cups cooked)
*   Chopped spinach
*   Basil leaves
*   Black pepper
*   Salt (optional/minimal)
*   Red pepper flakes (for topping)
*   Barley (optional, from barley tea, added instead of pasta)

**Optional additions:** oregano, parsley, sage, thyme, other white beans, carrots, celery, mushrooms, chard, kale (add broccoli/cauliflower towards the end to avoid mushiness).

**Method:**
1.  Sauté the red onion for a few minutes.
2.  Add watermelon rinds, collard stems, and garlic. Cook covered on low for 20 minutes or more until tender but still with a bite. (Tip: Watermelon rinds can be steamed for 15-20 minutes in an Instant Pot or pressure cooker first to soften).
3.  Add bell peppers, cooked white lima beans, black pepper, and salt. Cook until all are nicely done.
4.  Stir in chopped spinach and basil leaves.
5.  Top with red pepper flakes. Serve immediately for best taste.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text:
**Barley Tea Recipe:**
1.  Roast barley grains until they turn medium brown.
2.  Store in an airtight container once cooled.
3.  To make tea: Take 2 cups water and 2 tbsp roasted barley in a pot. Bring to a boil and steep on low for 5 minutes. Strain and enjoy. 

**Tip:** The leftover barley grains can be added to salads, soups, or eaten as is. Barley tea has a distinct flavor and is popular in Chinese, Japanese, and Korean cuisines, known for its health benefits.

recipe_name: Tip for Introducing New WFPB Ingredients
creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB
text: When introducing new ingredients into a WFPB diet, it's advisable to phase them in gradually, adding one or two new ingredients at a time. This helps the body adjust and can prevent issues like gas (e.g., from red grapes and prunes) or burning sensations (from very spicy peppers). The general rule of thumb is to start small when trying something new.

recipe_name: Frozen Tofu with Meaty Texture (Air-fried) & Stir-fry
creator: Prathima WFPB
text:
**Frozen Tofu Preparation:**
1.  Freeze firm tofu for 1-2 days.
2.  Defrost in the fridge for 1 day.
3.  Press out extra water using a cotton towel or weights.
4.  Chop tofu into desired shapes.

**Marinade:**
*   1 tsp corn flour
*   2-3 tsp water
*   1 tsp soy sauce
*   Pepper powder
*   1 tsp vinegar

**Air-frying Method:**
1.  Add chopped tofu to the marinade and let it sit for 15-30 minutes.
2.  Air-fry the marinated tofu for 8-10 minutes at 350°F (175°C) until crispy on the outside. Set aside.

**Stir-fry Application:**
1.  Chop plenty of onion, garlic, ginger, and green chili.
2.  On a well-heated pan, roast these chopped veggies along with bell peppers or other desired vegetables.
3.  Add the remaining marinade and the baked tofu.
4.  Add 1 tsp soy sauce if needed, and any seasoning of choice. For a lighter sweet taste, add 1/2 tsp dates paste or maple syrup.

text:
A recipe for a flavorful, crispy snack using mamra (puffed rice) and makhana (fox nuts). 

**Ingredients:**
*   Mamra
*   Makhana
*   Dry spices (of choice)
*   1-2 tbsp warm water or plant milk

**Method:**
1.  **Dry Roast the Base:** Roast mamra and makhana separately in a wide pan on low heat until crisp. Remove and set aside.
2.  **Prepare the Spice Coating:** In a small bowl, mix all desired dry spices together. Add 1–2 tbsp of warm water or plant milk to make a slightly thick, non-watery paste.
3.  **Coat Evenly:** Add the roasted mamra/makhana into a large mixing bowl. Sprinkle the spice paste on top and toss quickly and gently using a spatula or hands until everything is evenly coated. If too dry, spray or sprinkle a little more water and toss again.
4.  **Re-roast to Crisp Up:** Spread the mixture on a baking sheet or pan. Roast for 5–8 minutes in a preheated oven (300°F / 150°C) or on a low stove flame, stirring occasionally, until completely dry and crisp. The plant milk option is suggested for better sticking of spices.

creator: Group Member
text:
A collection of recipes and tips for cooking with fresh methi (fenugreek leaves):

**General Tip:** Always remove the tough, fibrous stems and only use the leaves, similar to mint.

**1. Methi with Purple Potatoes:** Cook/sauté methi with purple potatoes, choice of masala, and cumin seeds seasoning. Serve with rotis or rice.

**2. Methi Sambar:** A sambar incorporating methi, served with brown rice and quinoa.

**3. Methi Theplas and Parathas:** Add generous amounts of cleaned and chopped methi to flour before kneading the dough for theplas or parathas.

**4. Methi Waffles:** Soak and grind lentils, then add garlic, chili, spices, and loads of fine chopped methi. Cook in a waffle maker.

**5. Shalini's WFPB Methi Sabzi (Stuffed in Rotis):**
    *   **Ingredients:** Fresh methi (large amounts), mustard seeds, sesame seeds (generous), hing, coriander powder, turmeric, Kashmiri chili, water, roasted besan (optional).
    *   **Method:** Roast mustard and sesame seeds. Add hing, coriander powder, turmeric, and Kashmiri chili (add a few spoons of water immediately to prevent burning). Add cleaned and chopped methi. Stir, cover, and cook on medium-low for 25-30 minutes until soft. Optionally, add a couple of tablespoons of roasted besan at the end. Great for stuffing into rotis.

**6. Methi with Dal:** Methi tastes great cooked with split urad dal or split mung dal.

**7. Air-fried Methi Fritters:** Make fritters with chopped onions, finely diced potatoes, besan, and spices, then air-fry them.

**8. Methi Aloo:** A popular dish where potatoes are cooked directly with methi (not pre-boiled) for best taste.

recipe_name: Ethiopian Cooking: Berbere Spice Mix and Yellow Split Peas
creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text:
A detailed discussion on making Ethiopian dishes, highlighting the differences from Indian cuisine. The key difference lies in the use of yellow split peas (not chana dal), which cook to a creamy texture, and the specific proportions of spices in the Berbere spice mix. Ethiopian dishes are typically simply cooked, often without pre-made ginger-garlic paste or tomatoes. Vegetables are often steamed in the microwave for 10-12 minutes before sautéing.

**Berbere Spice Mix (as inferred from discussion):** Contains various spices, including (but not limited to) three types of chilies, allspice, and fenugreek powder. Shalini notes she often omits the three types of chilies (using Kashmiri chili powder instead), allspice, and fenugreek powder from her mix.

**Yellow Split Peas:** These are crucial for Ethiopian dishes and can be found in the bulk aisle of Whole Foods, large Indian stores, and mainstream grocery stores alongside other dried beans. They are also used in European cuisine, like French 'Potage Saint-Germain'.

Ankit Dangi WFPB shared that 'Kakdi ki sabzi' (cucumber, tomatoes, green chilies, curry leaves with spices) was a common dish growing up. The term 'Sinqua' was clarified to be ridge gourd or turai, and 'Turai-Kakdi ki sabzi' (ridge gourd and cucumber sabzi, usually without ridge gourd skin) is also common. There are various cucumber varieties in India, and no specific one was recommended for sabzi.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
Ingredients:
- 1 cup ash gourd (white pumpkin), diced
- ½ cup red cowpeas (vanpayar / red lobia), soaked overnight and cooked
- 1 small green chili, slit
- A few curry leaves
- Salt to taste (optional or minimal)

For the creamy base (coconut substitute):
- ¼ cup cooked brown rice or rolled oats
- 2 tbsp unsalted raw cashews or 2 tbsp cooked white beans (for nut-free)
- ¾–1 cup warm water

Instructions:
1. Cook cowpeas until soft and tender.
2. Cook ash gourd separately with green chili, curry leaves, and a splash of water until tender.
3. Blend the creamy base: Combine cooked rice (or oats), cashews (or white beans), and water. Blend until smooth and milky — this mimics the richness of coconut milk.
4. Add the creamy blend to the cooked vegetables and beans.
5. Simmer gently for 3–4 minutes to let flavors meld (do not boil hard).
6. Finish with a few fresh curry leaves for aroma.

text:
Serves 6-8 (or 4 plus leftovers).

Ingredients:
- 1 16-ounce bag brown lentils, rinsed and picked over
- 1 large tomato
- 1 medium red onion, peeled
- 1 leek, trimmed and washed
- 3 celery ribs, trimmed
- 1 small head of garlic
- 5 medium carrots, peeled and trimmed, divided
- 1 large white onion, finely chopped
- 2 tablespoons pimentón (Spanish smoked paprika) or more if you like
- 4 small potatoes, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch dice
- Kosher salt
- Sherry vinegar (optional)

Instructions:
1. Put the rinsed lentils in a large pot and cover with 4 cups of water. Add the tomato, red onion, leek, celery, garlic, and 2 of the carrots. Add more water if necessary, making sure all the vegetables are covered. Bring lentils and vegetables to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes. Occasionally skim the foam from the top of the boiling lentils and discard.
2. Separately, sauté the finely chopped white onion (without oil) and cook until golden and the onions just begin to caramelize, about 4 minutes. Add the pimentón (or whatever spices you have available) and stir until combined with the onions. Cook for about 30 seconds more then add the onions to the pot with the lentils and stir together until well combined. Continue to simmer the lentils for another 20 minutes.
3. Using tongs or a slotted spoon, carefully remove the celery, leek, tomato, garlic, and whole onion from the soup, and place them in a blender with some of the broth from the lentils. Puree the ingredients until smooth, then pour the mixture back into the pot and stir together with the lentils to thicken the soup.
4. Cut the remaining 3 carrots into 1/2-inch thick slices and add them, along with the potatoes, to the soup and continue cooking until the vegetables are soft and the lentils are tender, about 10 more minutes.
5. Season to taste with salt. Serve with an optional drizzle of sherry vinegar and a generous sprinkle of pimentón, if you like.

(Note: The original recipe included 3/4 cup of olive oil for sautéing, which was omitted for this WFPB adaptation.)

creator: Group Members
text:
Tips for maintaining a WFPB diet while traveling, especially in challenging environments like amusement parks:

**Planning & Packing:**
- Carry fruits, raw veggies (like carrots, celery), nuts, and dry snacks.
- Pack WFPB staples like Ezekiel bread, single-ingredient nut butters, and guacamole.
- Prepare rolled oats mixed with date powder and nut powder; in the hotel, just add hot water and mashed banana or frozen fruits.
- For flights, carry a medley of dried fruits and berries with dates, combine with rolled oats and water for a 'fruity oatmeal'. Enhance flavor with cacao, ginger, or cinnamon powder.

**Dining Out & In-Park Options:**
- Use apps like Happy Cow to find vegan restaurants in the area.
- Call ahead or check menus online to pre-decide on WFPB options.
- In parks, look for salads, rice/beans, or minimal-oil dishes like spaghetti.
- Inquire about dietary requirements to potentially carry a food bag into venues.

**Hotel/Airbnb Meal Ideas:**
- Utilize microwaves (common in hotels/Airbnbs) to cook whole sweet potatoes. Slice them and combine with canned beans (garbanzo, black, or red kidney beans) and a simple salsa (tomato, onion, cilantro, jalapeno, lemon, spice mix like All Purpose Seasoning or Trader Joe’s 21 Salute Seasoning). Add cucumber, tomatillo, or sliced grapes if available. Incorporate overnight-soaked dried berry medley for enhanced flavor.
- Wash and eat romaine lettuce raw, or chop and add to the sweet potato and bean preparation.

**Mindset & Flexibility:**
- It's okay to occasionally deviate from the diet during vacations. Enjoy the time with loved ones and resume WFPB eating upon return. The group offers support and encouragement for restarting.
- A resource titled 'Gently.. Start Again' (https://thankful2plants.plants.com/how-to/gently-start-again/index.html) is recommended for guidance on resuming healthy habits.
- One member shared their experience of driving for more flexibility, preparing large batches of WFPB meals for two days, and using apps to find vegan restaurants. They noted that completely avoiding salt, oil, and sugar was challenging and required a two-week readjustment period upon returning home.

text:
Ingredients:
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 1-2 small or medium tomatoes, finely chopped
- 1/2 cup finely chopped cilantro
- 1 large tablespoon powdered mixture of sesame seeds and roasted peanuts
- 1 heaping teaspoon of besan (chickpea flour)
- Turmeric powder, coriander powder, red chili powder, goda masala, hing (asafoetida)
- 1/2 cup water (or more, as needed)
- Thick-sliced karela (bitter gourd), slightly precooked in microwave for 3 mins
- Date powder (for sweetness)
- Lime juice (for sourness)
- Chaat masala (for garnish)

Method:
1. Precook thick-sliced karela by microwaving for 3 minutes.
2. In a bowl, mix the finely chopped onion, tomatoes, cilantro, sesame-peanut powder, besan, turmeric, coriander powder, red chili powder, goda masala, and hing. Add 1/2 cup water to form a curry base.
3. Combine the curry base with the precooked karela in a pressure cooker. Cook until 2 whistles on medium flame. Add a little more water if needed to prevent the curry from burning at the bottom.
4. Once cooked, add date powder and lime juice to taste, then sprinkle with chaat masala.

(Note: This dish is adapted from a traditional stuffed Karela recipe that typically uses oil for frying, dried coconut powder, kokum for sourness, and jaggery for sweetness. The red chili powder gives it a slightly red color, but the quantity can be adjusted for spice preference.)

creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB
text:
For the Dhokli:
- 1 cup whole wheat flour
- 1/3 cup besan (chickpea flour)
- 3-4 tbsp fennel seeds
- Turmeric powder, coriander powder, red chili powder, asafetida (hing), a pinch of salt
- Warm water (approx. 4-5 fl oz)

For the Dal:
- 1/2 cup green split moong dal
- 1/2 cup black split urad dal
- 1/3 cup chana dal
- Turmeric powder, asafetida
- 3-4 cups water

For the Tadka/Flavor Base:
- 2 tsp mustard seeds
- 2 tsp cumin seeds
- 1 red onion, chopped
- 8 garlic cloves, chopped
- 5 green chilies, chopped
- 1 inch ginger, chopped
- 2 tomatoes, chopped
- Turmeric powder, coriander powder, red chili powder
- Salt to taste
- Optional: a pinch or two of garam masala

For Serving:
- Cilantro, chopped
- Lemon juice
- 1 small red onion, chopped

Method:
1.  **Prepare the Dhokli:** Combine whole wheat flour, besan, fennel seeds, turmeric, coriander, red chili powder, asafetida, and salt. Knead the dough by gradually adding warm water (about 4-5 fl oz) until it's slightly wet. Cover and let the dough rest for 20 minutes. After resting, the dough will be less wet. Split the dough into pieces. Take small, bite-sized pieces and flatten them into circular shapes using your index fingers and thumb. Alternatively, roll the dough like a roti and cut into diamond shapes with a pizza cutter, or use a bottle cap/cookie cutter. (Pasta can be used as a substitute for dhokli to save time).
2.  **Prepare the Dal:** While the dough rests, soak green split moong dal, black split urad dal, and chana dal for about 15 minutes. Pressure cook the soaked dals with turmeric powder and asafetida for 3 whistles.
3.  **Assemble Dal Dhokli:** After opening the pressure cooker, turn on the stove, add 3-4 cups of water to the dal, and bring it to a boil. Gradually add the dhokli pieces one by one to the boiling dal (do not add all at once to prevent sticking). Let it boil on medium flame, allowing the dhokli to rise to the top. Gently stir occasionally to prevent dhokli from sticking to the bottom and remove any foam/froth that forms.
4.  **Prepare the Tadka:** In a separate saucepan, water sauté mustard and cumin seeds. Add the chopped red onion, garlic, green chilies, ginger, and tomatoes. Sauté until softened. Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder.
5.  **Finish the Dish:** When most of the dhokli have risen to the top, add the contents of the saucepan (tadka) to the dal and dhokli in the cooker. Let it simmer for about 5-10 minutes for the flavors to blend. Add salt to taste and red chili powder for a distinctive tadka-like color. Optionally, add a pinch or two of garam masala. Stir, turn off the stove, and top with chopped cilantro.
6.  **Serve:** With each serving, top with fresh lemon juice and chopped red onions. (Traditionally, it's also cherished with a red spicy garlic chutney, but this is skipped for a WFPBNO preparation.)

creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB
text:
This recipe for Rajasthani-style Dal Dhokli is WFPBNO (Whole Food Plant-Based No Oil).

**For the Dhokli:**
*   **Ingredients:** 1 cup whole wheat flour, 1/3 cup besan (chickpea flour), 3-4 tbsp fennel seeds, turmeric powder, coriander powder, red chili powder, asafetida, a pinch of salt, 4-5 fl oz warm water (gradually added).
*   **Method:** Knead the dough by gradually adding warm water until it's a bit wet (besan absorbs water when rested). Cover and let the dough rest for 20 minutes. The dough will no longer be wet. Split the dough into three pieces and roll them. Take small bite-size pieces and flatten them into circular shapes using index fingers and thumb, placing them on a plate to prevent sticking. To save time, you can roll the dough like a roti and cut diamond shapes with a pizza cutter, or use a bottle cap/small cookie cutter for circular shapes. Alternatively, pasta can be used as a shortcut for the dhoklis.

**For the Dal:**
*   **Ingredients:** 1/2 cup green split moong dal, 1/2 cup black split urad dal (correction from original message), 1/3 cup chana dal, turmeric powder, asafetida, 3-4 cups water.
*   **Method:** Soak the dals for about 15 minutes. Pressure cook them for 3 whistles with turmeric powder and asafetida. After opening the lid, turn on the stove, add 3-4 cups of water to the dal, and bring it to a boil. Gradually add the prepared dhoklis one by one to the cooker to prevent them from sticking together. Let it boil on a medium flame, allowing the dhoklis to rise to the top. Gently stir occasionally to unsettle any dhoklis that have settled at the bottom, and remove any foam/froth that forms.

**For the Tempering/Sauce:**
*   **Ingredients:** 2 tsp mustard seeds, 2 tsp cumin seeds, 1 red onion (chopped), 8 garlic cloves (chopped), 5 green chillies (chopped), 1 inch ginger (chopped), 2 tomatoes (chopped), turmeric powder, coriander powder, red chili powder. (Adjust quantities to taste). Also, 1 more small red onion (chopped) for serving.
*   **Method:** In a saucepan, water sauté the mustard and cumin seeds. Add the chopped red onion, garlic, green chillies, ginger, and tomatoes, along with turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Sauté until softened.

**Assembly and Finishing:**
*   When almost all the dhoklis have risen to the top (like pasta), add the contents of the saucepan to the cooker with the dal and dhokli. Let it simmer for about 5-10 minutes for the flavors to blend. Add salt to taste and red chili powder for a distinctive tadka-like color. Optionally, add a pinch or two of garam masala (not added in this recipe). Stir, turn off the stove, and top with fresh cilantro. Serve each portion topped with lemon juice and chopped red onions. Traditionally, it's served with a red spicy garlic chutney, but this is skipped for WFPBNO.

creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB, Gurmeet Singh Manku, Group Member (WFPB member)
text:
Teff is a tiny whole grain, technically a grass, similar to millets and wild rice. Injera, a fermented teff crepe, is a common dish in Ethiopian cuisine.

**Stovetop Cooking Method (Ankit Dangi WFPB):**
*   **Ingredients:** 1/2 cup raw teff, 2 cups water, cacao powder (to taste), unsweetened soy milk (optional), fruits (for topping).
*   **Method:** Boil 1/2 cup raw teff with 2 cups of water for 12-15 minutes on medium flame. A lid is not needed. Stir every 4-5 minutes. Towards the end, add cacao powder and mix well. Optionally, add unsweetened soy milk. Serve topped with fruits.

**Microwave Cooking Notes (Gurmeet Singh Manku):**
*   Teff can be heated in the microwave without sputtering, even without a cover, though a microwave splatter cover is handy and habitually used.
*   Soaking water is not discarded, and water is added by intuition rather than precise measurement.

**Stovetop Soaking/Rinsing (Group Member WFPB member):**
*   Rinse soaked teff and use double the water for stovetop cooking.

**Teff Texture and Idli (Gurmeet Singh Manku):**
*   When cooked as described, teff forms a thick porridge that crumbles rather than sticking together like idli. Teff idli can be made via fermentation with urad dal and fenugreek seeds, similar to idlis made with other whole grains.

recipe_name: Whole Green Gram and Whole Black Urad Dal Idli
creator: Ashwini Vikram
text:
This recipe makes idlis without rice, using only dals.

**Ingredients:** 1 cup whole green gram, 1/2 cup whole black urad dal, 1 tsp methi (fenugreek) seeds.

**Method:**
1.  Soak the whole green gram and whole black urad dal with methi seeds for about 6 hours.
2.  Grind the dals separately. (Grinding urad dal and green gram together can be problematic as urad dal grinds faster and starts to rise while green gram is still processing).
3.  Use very little water while grinding to ensure the batter has the right consistency for idlis.
4.  Mix the ground batters together and let them ferment overnight.
5.  Steam the idlis longer than regular white idlis.

recipe_name: Baked Eggplant Roundels and Grilled Pineapple
creator: Kusum WFPB
text:
This recipe provides methods for preparing baked eggplant and grilled pineapple.

**Grilled Pineapple:**
*   Use a cast iron grill pan. Heat it on high to get good grill marks, then lower the heat slightly to cook the pineapples without overcooking them.

**Baked Eggplant Roundels:**
*   **Preparation:** Sprinkle salt lightly on eggplant roundels and leave them on a cutting board for about an hour. This allows the eggplants to release water, which helps them retain their shape during cooking. (Skipping this step can cause them to lose shape).
*   **Coating:** Grind 1 toasted Ezekiel bread into coarse breadcrumbs. Mix with powdered spices such as smoked paprika, garlic powder, turmeric, black pepper, amchur powder, and some chaat masala. Mix all ingredients well.
*   **Method:** Spread the spice mixture on a plate and coat all eggplant slices thoroughly. Bake in the oven at 350°F (175°C) for 30 minutes, turning them once halfway through. Baking is preferred over pan-cooking as pan-cooked eggplant can break or not cook well with frequent turning.

text:

1.  Wash the curry leaves (or mint/methi). For mint and methi, chop them before drying.
2.  Dry them thoroughly with a kitchen towel.

1.  For a large quantity (e.g., 1lb bag), microwave in batches.
2.  Once microwaved and dried, grind the leaves in a blender.
3.  The ground leaves can then be added to dishes like cooked rice, along with other seasonings like onion powder, asafetida, and cooked peanuts.

text:
This is a unique rasam recipe using cranberries, suitable for those avoiding tamarind and tomatoes.

**Ingredients:**
*   1/2 cup cranberries
*   1/2 cup water
*   1/2 tsp cumin seeds
*   1/2 tsp black pepper
*   1/2 tsp coriander seeds
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp salt
*   1/2 tsp ginger
*   1/2 tsp green chili
*   1/2 tsp curry leaves
*   1/2 tsp mustard seeds
*   1/2 tsp asafetida
*   1/2 tsp lemon juice

**Method:**
1.  Boil cranberries in 1/2 cup water for 5 minutes.
2.  Blend all ingredients together except mustard seeds, asafetida, and lemon juice.
3.  Add the blended mixture to the boiled cranberries.
4.  Bring the mixture to a boil.
5.  Add mustard seeds and asafetida.
6.  Simmer for 5 minutes.
7.  Stir in lemon juice just before serving. Serve hot.

text:
This discussion covers experiences with home mushroom growing kits and cooking tips for oyster mushrooms.

**Mushroom Growing Kits:**
*   **Source:** Fungi Farms Gourmet mushrooms (https://www.thefungifarms.com/) was mentioned as a brand available at farmers markets.
*   **Disposal:** To discard a mushroom growing kit, separate the organic growing medium (substrate) from its packaging. The substrate can be composted or used as a garden amendment. Packaging (plastic bag, cardboard box) should be disposed of according to local recycling guidelines. If the kit has unusual molds, spray the contaminated area with bleach or Lysol, seal the block in a plastic bag, and dispose of in general waste to prevent spore spread. Clean tools and surfaces thoroughly.

**Oyster Mushroom Cooking Tips:**
*   **Searing:** A favorite method is to sear oyster mushrooms (like snow oysters) between two heavy cast iron skillets with just a few seasonings. A panini maker could achieve a similar effect.
*   **Usage:** Oyster mushrooms can be added to noodles, soups, and other dishes.

recipe_name: Strategies for Increased Leafy Greens Consumption
creator: Ankit Dangi WFPB, Group Member (WFPB member), Group Member (WFPB member)
text:
This discussion explores practical strategies for consistently consuming leafy greens multiple times a day, as recommended by Dr. Esselstyn for heart health and blood pressure management.

**Strategies Shared:**
1.  **Integrate into Traditional Meals:** Lean heavily on Indian dishes like saag, dal palak, and aloo methi to include greens in each meal without extra effort.
2.  **Easy Snacking:** Keep an easy dressing and a mixture of roasted 'parm' (pepitas, walnuts, nutritional yeast) readily available for quick snacks with greens.
3.  **Convenience:** Use pre-washed greens to reduce preparation friction.
4.  **Raw Consumption:** Eat arugula, spinach, or other greens straight out of the bag (Essy style).
5.  **Air-Fried Kale Chips:** Make air-fried kale chips seasoned with cheesy nutritional yeast.
6.  **Creative Plating:** Plate main meals on a bed of greens (e.g., Mac and cheese on spinach) and generously use lettuce or kale in sandwiches.
7.  **Accessible Tools:** Keep a steamer on the kitchen counter to reduce friction for steaming greens.
8.  **Steamed Greens for Snacking:** Steam leafy greens, store them in the fridge, and snack on them with balsamic vinegar.
9.  **Light Meals:** Prepare light meals like steamed broccoli rabe with soaked and cooked fava beans.
10. **Salads:** Make salads with steamed leafy greens, beets, and other vegetables.
11. **Nitric Oxide Rich Dishes:** Incorporate dishes like methi sambar, which contain ingredients known to produce nitric oxide.

recipe_name: Discussion: Simple Meals vs. Complex Recipes
creator: Group Member (WFPB member), Ankit Dangi WFPB, Kumar Natarajan Satvic, Group Member (WFPB member)
text:
This discussion explores the preference for simple meals versus complex recipes, touching on laziness, familiarity, and nutritional value.

**Key Points:**
*   **Appreciation for Simplicity:** Some members find satisfaction in simple meals, appreciating the unique taste of individual vegetables, greens, or herbs without complicated spices or sauces. Examples include plain steamed sweet potatoes, cooked whole wheat and toor dal with salt/turmeric, tofu cubes in kimchi, or simple tofu wraps.
*   **Role of Spices:** While simple meals are valued, it's acknowledged that herbs and spices offer significant nutritional value (e.g., cinnamon, lemon) that cannot be obtained elsewhere.
*   **Challenges with Spices:** Many people, including experienced cooks, admit to not fully understanding spices—how much to use, which ingredients to pair them with, different forms, flavor composition changes with vegetables, and cooking times. This unfamiliarity often leads to avoiding them or relying on predefined spice mixes/recipes with measured amounts.
*   **Familiarity vs. Experimentation:** Predefined spice mixes work well with familiar ingredients (e.g., chole masala with chickpeas). However, with newer ingredients (e.g., radicchio and fava beans), it's harder to gauge spice usage, leading to reliance on simple pairings like black pepper, salt, and lemon juice.
*   **'Laziness' and Curiosity:** The preference for simple meals can stem from a lack of interest or time to experiment with new ingredients. However, it's suggested that 'simplicity' is often a result of repetition; a meal that seems difficult initially becomes simple after being made repeatedly. The group encourages curiosity and experimentation, as one never knows what might become a favorite and a 'simple' staple (e.g., Teff grain with fruits and cacao powder).

creator: Gurmeet
text:
To discard a mushroom growing kit, separate the organic growing medium (substrate) from its packaging. The substrate is rich in nutrients and can be composted by breaking it into pieces and adding to a home compost bin or worm farm. Alternatively, use it as garden mulch by scattering it onto garden beds or around potted plants; bonus mushrooms may grow after rain. For some species, burying the block in a shaded garden area can encourage further natural flushes, but check species-specific guidance (e.g., Lion's Mane strains could out-compete wild UK varieties, requiring proper disposal to protect local ecosystems).

Packaging: The plastic liner bag is typically not curbside recyclable and should go into general waste. The outer cardboard box can be flattened and recycled.

Special Considerations for Contaminated Kits: If the kit develops unusual green, black, or red molds (like trichoderma), take extra care. Spray the contaminated area with a bleach solution or Lysol before handling to minimize spore spread. Seal the entire contaminated block in a plastic bag before placing it in the general garbage bin; avoid composting to prevent introducing contaminants to your garden. Thoroughly clean any surfaces, tubs, or tools that touched the contaminated kit with a disinfectant like 70% rubbing alcohol or bleach solution.

creator: WFPB member
text:
Tips and recipes for incorporating more leafy greens:

**General Tips:**
*   Kale holds best in the fridge among leafy greens. A combination of Kale, Swiss chard, and Arugula is often used.
*   Steam leafy greens and store them in the fridge for easy snacking with Balsamic vinegar.
*   Make salads with steamed leafy greens, beets, and other vegetables.
*   Methi sambar is a favorite for its Nitric Oxide producing ingredients.
*   **Caution:** Be aware of potential adverse reactions to large amounts of spinach due to oxalates.

**Quick Broccoli Rabe + Fava Beans Sauté:**
*   **Ingredients:** Fava beans (soaked overnight), Broccoli Rabe (chopped into one-inch pieces), water, light salt, toasted seeds or nuts (for crunch).
*   **Method:** On a pan, sauté the Broccoli Rabe with water. If fava beans are on the tougher side after soaking, start sautéing them first. Add the remaining ingredients and salt. Top with any crunchy toasted seeds or nuts.

**Methi Sambar:**
*   **Ingredients:** Finely chopped cleaned methi leaves (cut off tough stem ends if needed), mixed dals (Chana, Toor, Moong dals, cooked with turmeric), tamarind water (start with a small amount, e.g., half the size of a golf ball), sambar masala powder, salt (if desired), dry tadka (mustard seeds, asafoetida, small red chili, curry leaves).
*   **Method:** Cook the dals with turmeric. In a pot large enough for sambar (3-4x dal volume), sauté the chopped methi leaves in water until tender. Add salt. Add tamarind water and cook methi halfway. Add sambar masala powder and cook for another 5-8 minutes. Add the cooked dal and let it simmer until it bubbles up. Prepare a dry tadka with mustard seeds, asafoetida, small red chili, and curry leaves, and add it to the sambar. Enjoy with brown rice or quinoa.

recipe_name: Identifying Sugar Crystals vs. Mold on Dried Figs
creator: Gurmeet
text:
White specks on sun-dried figs are usually natural sugar crystals (often called sugar bloom), which are normal, very common, and safe to eat. As figs dry, their natural sugars migrate to the surface and crystallize.
*   **Sugar crystals:** Look dry, chalky, or grainy; are evenly scattered; feel hard or slightly gritty if rubbed; and have no off smell.
*   **Mold (not safe):** Appears fuzzy or hairy; forms blue, green, or gray patches; has a musty or sour smell; and feels soft or slimy underneath.
*   **Tip:** If the texture of the sugar crystals is bothersome, soak the figs in warm water for 5–10 minutes, and the crystals will dissolve.

recipe_name: Stove-top Cooking for Dals and Beans (vs. Pressure Cooker)
creator: Group Member
text:
For cooking dals and beans, presoaking for some time and then boiling on the stove is suggested as an alternative to pressure cooking. This method is believed to result in a 'tad better' taste and potentially preserve nutrients by avoiding the higher temperatures of a pressure cooker. For dals like moong dal, stove-top cooking after soaking takes only 10-15 minutes.

For tougher beans, soaking for 10-12 hours, changing the water a few times, and using warm water can speed up the process. The Instant Pot's chili/bean mode (which uses lower pressure) is also recommended as a good compromise, preventing overcooking of fibers and loss of texture compared to full pressure cooking.
